3. It aims to train 20 lakh grassroots Adi Karmayogis across one lakh tribal villages.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan is a Central Sector initiative of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. It envisages training 20 lakh grassroots Adi Karmayogis across one lakh tribal villages.
6.tq: Combine ministry, scheme type and numerical targets, checking whether all three statements fit the same programme.

6.s:
Project BHISHM is primarily associated with which of the following?

1. Portable cubes functioning as mobile hospitals
2. The Aarogya Maitri initiative
3. Provision of two such cubes to Sri Lanka

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
6.x: Project BHISHM, under Aarogya Maitri, consists of portable cubes that function as mobile hospitals. Two such cubes were given to Sri Lanka.
6.tq: Use the scheme’s distinctive equipment, parent initiative and international recipient as linked clues.

6.s: The Immigration, Visa, Foreigners Registration and Tracking (IVFRT) programme is implemented by which combination?
o: Bureau of Immigration and National Informatics Centre
Bureau of Police Research and Development and UIDAI
6.x: IVFRT is under the Ministry of Home Affairs and is implemented through the Bureau of Immigration and the National Informatics Centre. Its extension is up to March 2031.
6.tq: Start from the sure implementing-agency pair and reject agencies belonging to neighbouring schemes.

6.s: The PM SVANidhi scheme is associated with which implementing agency?
6.x: PM SVANidhi is associated with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and the Department of Financial Services, with SIDBI as the implementing agency.
6.tq: Identify the implementing institution rather than the nodal ministry.

6.s: GOBARdhan, now known as the National Circular Bioenergy Scheme, was moved to which Union Ministry?
o: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
6.x: GOBARdhan was moved to the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. The scheme received an approved outlay of ₹23,731 crore for FY 2027–FY 2036.
6.tq: Apply the ‘which ministry’ trap by distinguishing the present ministry from related rural and renewable-energy ministries.

6.s: MY Bharat was launched on 31 October 2023 as a replacement for which organisation?
6.x: MY Bharat was launched on 31 October 2023 under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, replacing the Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan, established in 1972.
6.tq: Use the launch date and predecessor organisation to distinguish the youth programme from similar bodies.

6.s: Rashtriya Uchchतर Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA), concerning higher education, now continues in which form?
6.x: RUSA, the higher-education scheme of the Ministry of Human Resource Development, now continues as PM-USHA. PM-USHA links central grants with compliance with NEP 2020.
6.tq: Discriminate between similarly named education programmes by matching the higher-education scheme with its successor.

6.s: Which of the following States is NOT included among the eastern States covered by the PURVODAYA development plan?
6.x: PURVODAYA covers Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. Chhattisgarh is not included in this listed group.
6.tq: Find the outsider by checking every option against the complete geographical list.

6.s: Which one of the following was added to PURVODAYA in Budget 2026–27?
o: A Himalayan Industrial Corridor with a node at Dehradun
A North-East Industrial Corridor with a node at Guwahati
An East Coast Industrial Corridor with a node at Durgapur
A West Coast Industrial Corridor with a node at Surat
6.x: Budget 2026–27 added an East Coast Industrial Corridor with a node at Durgapur to the PURVODAYA framework. It also provided for five tourism destinations and 4,000 e-buses.
6.tq: Use the location-and-node pair as the decisive clue in a scheme-feature question.

6.s: Khelo India was originally launched in which year?
6.x: The Khelo India programme was launched in 2018. Its later revision includes feeder schools, Utkrishta Vidyalayas and a target of making India a top-ten sporting nation by 2036.
6.tq: Test the launch year directly using closely spaced chronological distractors.

6.s: Under the revised Khelo India arrangements, infrastructure costs are generally shared in which ratio, with a special ratio for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States?
o: 90:10 generally and 60:40 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States
60:40 generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States
50:50 generally and 75:25 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States
75:25 generally and 60:40 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States
6.x: Khelo India infrastructure costs are shared in a 60:40 ratio in general, while the ratio is 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States.
6.tq: Separate the general funding ratio from the special regional ratio before comparing options.

6.s: Which of the following is a new feature associated with the revamped Khelo India programme?
o: PM Sports Universities exclusively for each district
6.x: Khelo India Feeder Schools and Utkrishta Vidyalayas are new features of the revamped programme. The programme also targets India’s emergence as a top-ten sporting nation by 2036.
6.tq: Identify the exact official programme term rather than a plausible but non-existent institutional label.

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding MISHTI:
1. MISHTI stands for Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes.
2. It has been extended up to 2029.
3. Its total outlay after the additional allocation is ₹600 crore.
4. Andhra Pradesh ranked second among the States under the initiative.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: MISHTI expands to Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes. It has been extended to 2029, received ₹500 crore more to reach a total of ₹600 crore, and Andhra Pradesh ranked second among States.
6.tq: Check the acronym, extension year, revised outlay and State ranking as separate factual components.

6.s: Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan was launched by President Pranab Mukherjee on 9 July 2015 with the objective of promoting which subjects among school children?
6.x: Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan was launched by President Pranab Mukherjee on 9 July 2015 to promote science and mathematics among school children.
6.tq: Link the launching authority, date and objective without confusing the target subjects.

6.s: Unnat Bharat Abhiyan seeks to establish a functional link between higher educational institutions and which of the following?
6.x: Unnat Bharat Abhiyan, associated with the Ministry of Human Resource Development, links IITs, NITs and IISERs with villages.
6.tq: Infer the programme’s target area from the stated institutional-to-community linkage.

6.s: Har Ghar Tiranga 2026 was launched by which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
6.x: Har Ghar Tiranga 2026 was launched by the Ministry of Culture. It was scheduled from 9 to 17 August 2026 under the theme ‘Spirit of Vande Mataram’, including the SURYAPATH TIRANGA flag relay across Indian Missions.
6.tq: Use the launching ministry as the primary discriminator in a current-affairs scheme question.

6.s: The Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan primarily targets which group?
6.x: The campaign targets drug-free youth. It is associated with the Prime Minister and the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through MY Bharat, and follows a 100-week Jan Bhagidari plan based on the Kashi Declaration.
6.tq: Match the campaign’s name with its clearly specified target group and implementing channel.

6.s: The Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra was launched from Khunti in Jharkhand on which date?
6.x: The Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra was launched by the Prime Minister on 15 November 2023 at Khunti, Jharkhand, with the objective of achieving last-mile saturation of government schemes.
6.tq: Combine place, date and objective to avoid confusing this yatra with other national campaigns.

6.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Nayi Disha — Delhi Police initiative to bring school dropouts back
2. Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan — Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
3. Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan — implemented through the National Institute of Social Defence

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
6.x: Nayi Disha is a Delhi Police initiative for bringing school dropouts back. Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan is associated with the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and is run through the National Institute of Social Defence.
6.tq: Match each campaign with its implementing body and purpose before selecting the code.

6.s: The Jal Jeevan Mission was launched in which year?
6.x: The Jal Jeevan Mission was launched in 2019 under the Ministry of Jal Shakti. It has been extended to December 2028 to cover all 19.36 crore rural households.
6.tq: Test the launch year using adjacent years as chronological distractors.

6.s: Which ministry is associated with the Jal Jeevan Mission?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
6.x: The Jal Jeevan Mission is administered by the Ministry of Jal Shakti. Its revised outlay is ₹8.69 lakh crore and its coverage target is all rural households by December 2028.
6.tq: Apply the ‘who handles this subject’ method to distinguish the water ministry from related ministries.

6.s: Under the Jal Jeevan Mission, the funding pattern for the Himalayan and North-Eastern States is:
6.x: The Jal Jeevan Mission follows a 90:10 funding pattern for the Himalayan and North-Eastern States. For other States, the pattern is 50:50.
6.tq: Separate regional funding exceptions from the general funding pattern.

6.s: Gyan Bharatam Mission, announced in July 2025, is administered by which ministry?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
6.x: Gyan Bharatam Mission is administered by the Ministry of Culture. It has an outlay of ₹491.66 crore for 2025–31 and aims to digitise more than one crore manuscripts.
6.tq: Match the manuscript-preservation objective with the appropriate cultural ministry.

6.s: What is the primary objective of the Gyan Bharatam Mission?
o: To establish one crore public libraries
To translate all school textbooks into regional languages
To digitise land records in one crore villages
To digitise more than one crore manuscripts
6.x: The Gyan Bharatam Mission aims to digitise more than one crore manuscripts. The National Manuscript Survey recorded 1.19 crore manuscripts by March 2026.
6.tq: Distinguish the exact object of digitisation from other cultural and administrative digitisation programmes.

6.s: The target period of the National Quantum Mission is:
6.x: The National Quantum Mission is implemented by the Department of Science and Technology for the period 2023–24 to 2030–31. It envisages quantum machines ranging from 50 to 1,000 qubits.
6.tq: Read the beginning and terminal years carefully, especially where the period spans multiple financial years.

6.s: The National Quantum Mission envisages the development of quantum machines in which range?
6.x: The National Quantum Mission targets quantum machines in the range of 50 to 1,000 qubits. It is associated with the Department of Science and Technology.
6.tq: Test the quantitative range directly, using scale-based distractors from the same subject area.

6.s: Which of the following correctly describes the present structure of the Swachh Bharat Mission?
o: Only SBM-G Phase II is continuing
SBM-G Phase I and SBM-U 1.0 are continuing without revision
SBM-G Phase II and SBM-U 2.0 are continuing
6.x: The Swachh Bharat Mission, launched on 2 October 2014, now operates through SBM-G Phase II and SBM-U 2.0. It is associated with the Ministry of Jal Shakti and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
6.tq: Distinguish the current phases from the original launch phase by focusing on the suffixes and sector labels.

6.s: APAAR is the acronym for:
6.x: APAAR stands for Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry. It is the Ministry of Education’s lifelong student identification system.
6.tq: Expand the exact official acronym, rejecting plausible substitutions of the key words.

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding APAAR:
1. It is a lifelong student ID associated with the Ministry of Education.
2. It is linked to the Academic Bank of Credits.
3. The Academic Bank of Credits has 2,963 registered institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: APAAR is the Ministry of Education’s lifelong student ID and is linked to the Academic Bank of Credits. The Academic Bank of Credits has 2,963 registered institutions.
6.tq: Check the identity system, its linked platform and the supporting numerical fact together.

6.s: NSQF stands for:
6.x: NSQF means National Skills Qualification Framework. Skill India certificates are mapped to NSQF and linked to DigiLocker.
6.tq: Discriminate between similar expansions by retaining the exact terms ‘Skills’ and ‘Qualification’.

6.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between Skill India certificates and NSQF?
o: Skill India certificates are mapped to NSQF and linked to DigiLocker.
Skill India certificates are issued only through the Academic Bank of Credits.
NSQF certificates cannot be linked to any digital repository.
NSQF is used exclusively for school examination certificates.
6.x: Skill India certificates are mapped to the National Skills Qualification Framework and linked to DigiLocker. NSQF is not limited to school examinations or the Academic Bank of Credits.
6.tq: Apply the framework’s practical function rather than merely expanding its acronym.

6.s: VB-G RAM G is the abbreviated form of which programme?
o: Village Bharat - Gram Rozgar and Agriculture Mission (Gramin)
Viksit Bharat - Guaranteed Rural Assets Mission (General)
Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)
Vikas Bharat - Gram Ration and Awas Mission (Gramin)
6.x: VB-G RAM G expands to Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin).
6.tq: Expand each acronym segment in sequence and reject look-alike substitutions.

6.s: Sampada is best described as which of the following?
o: A property e-registration portal of Madhya Pradesh
6.x: Sampada is the property e-registration portal of Madhya Pradesh. It is distinct from APAAR, DigiLocker and water-sector portals.
6.tq: Identify the portal’s State and administrative purpose instead of being misled by its generic name.

6.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Noida International Airport at Jewar?
o: It is a privately owned airport established exclusively for international cargo
It is a public-private partnership project and a net-zero airport whose Phase 1 was opened by the Prime Minister
It is a wholly government-owned airport and India’s first airport in a Special Economic Zone
It is India’s first railway-linked airport developed under the BOT model
6.x: The Noida International Airport at Jewar is being developed as a public-private partnership and is described as a net-zero airport. Its first phase was opened by the Prime Minister.
6.tq: Use the project-description combination rather than being distracted by ownership or model swaps.

6.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bairabi-Sairang is Mizoram’s first railway line.
2. Aizawl became the fourth capital in the North-East to be placed on the railway map.
3. Bairabi-Sairang is India’s first major river-linking project.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: Bairabi-Sairang is Mizoram’s first railway line, and Aizawl is the fourth North-Eastern capital on the rail map. The first major river-linking project is Ken-Betwa, not Bairabi-Sairang.
6.tq: Separate the railway facts from the river-linking fact to identify the wrong statement.

6.s: The first Vande Bharat Sleeper depot is located at:
6.x: Bhagat Ki Kothi in Jodhpur is the location of the first Vande Bharat Sleeper depot.
6.tq: Test the exact location associated with an infrastructure first.

6.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Ken-Betwa project is correct?
o: It is a net-zero airport project implemented through a public-private partnership.
It is Mizoram’s first railway project and faces protests over land acquisition.
It is the first foreign university campus project in India.
It is India’s first major river-linking project and faces protests relating to displacement.
6.x: Ken-Betwa is India’s first major river-linking project, and displacement protests have been associated with it.
6.tq: Match the project with its distinctive first and associated issue.

6.s: Foreign university campuses in India are established under which regulatory framework?
6.x: Foreign university campuses are set up under the University Grants Commission Regulations, 2023.
6.tq: Identify the correct regulatory authority and year instead of a neighbouring education framework.

6.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Project or institution)
a. FIU-IND–I4C
b. FIU-IND–SEBI
c. India–France cooperation

d. Andhra Pradesh Government–Kia India

List-II (Purpose)
i. ITI at Penukonda
 ii. Aeronautics skilling centre at NSTI Kanpur
 iii. Prevention of cyber-financial fraud
 iv. Anti-money laundering

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
6.x: FIU-IND and I4C cooperate to stop cyber-financial fraud; FIU-IND and SEBI cooperate on anti-money laundering; India-France cooperation concerns an aeronautics skilling centre at NSTI Kanpur; and the Andhra Pradesh Government–Kia India arrangement concerns an ITI at Penukonda.
6.tq: Start from the sure partner-purpose pair and eliminate codes containing a swapped purpose.

6.s: The India-France cooperation mentioned in connection with skilling is associated with the establishment of a centre at:
6.x: The India-France arrangement concerns an aeronautics skilling centre at NSTI Kanpur.
6.tq: Discriminate between the partner, institution and purpose in an MoU.

6.s: The Andhra Pradesh Government–Kia India arrangement is associated with which of the following?
o: A ₹12 crore aeronautics centre at Kanpur
A ₹12 crore ITI at Penukonda under corporate social responsibility
A ₹120 crore railway line between Bairabi and Sairang
6.x: The Andhra Pradesh Government and Kia India arrangement concerns a ₹12 crore ITI at Penukonda under CSR.
6.tq: Pair the company with the correct state project and amount.

6.s: The headquarters of the National Turmeric Board is located at:
6.x: The National Turmeric Board, set up in January 2025, has its headquarters at Nizamabad in Telangana.
6.tq: Use location-based elimination among headquarters of national institutions.

6.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Turmeric Board was set up in January 2025.
2. Its headquarters is at Nizamabad in Telangana.
3. The National Makhana Board is associated with Bihar.
4. The Central Sector scheme for makhana has an outlay of ₹476.03 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: All four statements are correct. The Turmeric Board was set up in January 2025 at Nizamabad, while the Makhana Board is associated with Bihar and its Central Sector scheme has an outlay of ₹476.03 crore.
6.tq: Check each institution against its place, date and financial figure before selecting the combined code.

6.s: The rules relating to the National Sports Board and National Sports Tribunal were notified in May 2026 under the:
6.x: The rules for the National Sports Board and National Sports Tribunal were notified in May 2026 under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025.
6.tq: Match the subordinate rules with the correct parent legislation and year.

6.s: Under PM-KISAN, eligible landholding farmer families receive:
o: ₹6,000 annually in two instalments of ₹3,000 each
₹6,000 annually in three instalments of ₹2,000 each
₹12,000 annually in three instalments of ₹4,000 each
6.x: PM-KISAN provides ₹6,000 per year to eligible landholding farmer families in three instalments of ₹2,000 each.
6.tq: Break the total benefit into its instalment structure.

6.s: Which of the following categories is excluded from PM-KISAN as indicated in the scheme features?
o: Income-tax payers and most government employees
Small and marginal farmers without income-tax liability
Farmer families receiving the benefit through bank accounts
6.x: Income-tax payers and most government employees are excluded from PM-KISAN, while the scheme covers eligible landholding farmer families.
6.tq: Find the exception by distinguishing the beneficiary group from excluded categories.

6.s: Which one of the following correctly describes VB-G RAM G?
o: It provides 125 days of work to rural households with an interim base wage of ₹300 per day.
It provides 100 days of work to urban households with a base wage of ₹500 per day.
It provides 150 days of work to farmers with a yearly benefit of ₹6,000.
It provides subsidised LPG connections to adult women in rural households.
6.x: VB-G RAM G provides 125 days of work to rural households and specifies an interim base wage of ₹300 per day.
6.tq: Distinguish an employment guarantee feature from farmer and LPG benefits.

6.s: Under VB-G RAM G, wages are shared between the Centre and States in which ratio?
6.x: The wages under VB-G RAM G are shared between the Centre and States in the ratio of 60:40.
6.tq: Test the precise fiscal-sharing ratio rather than the number of workdays.

6.s: The loan structure under PM SVANidhi is correctly represented by:
6.x: PM SVANidhi provides successive loans of ₹15,000, ₹25,000 and ₹50,000 to street vendors.
6.tq: Recall the ascending three-stage loan sequence exactly.

6.s:
Consider the following statements about PM SVANidhi:
1. It is meant for street vendors.
2. It provides a 7% interest subsidy.
3. The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and the Department of Financial Services are associated with it.
4. SIDBI implements the scheme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: All four statements are correct. PM SVANidhi targets street vendors, provides a 7% interest subsidy, involves MoHUA and DFS, and is implemented by SIDBI.
6.tq: Verify the beneficiary, subsidy and institutional roles before choosing the all-inclusive code.

6.s: PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana is intended primarily to promote:
o: Employment of first-time employees through EPFO
Procurement of pulses at minimum support price
6.x: PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana is linked with EPFO and aims to generate 3.5 crore jobs, particularly benefiting first-time employees.
6.tq: Match the scheme with its target group and implementation channel.

6.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: PMUY — ₹5 lakh health cover per family per year
PM-JAY — ₹5 lakh per poor family per year
PM-KISAN — ₹300 daily wage for rural workers
PM SVANidhi — free property cards for street vendors
6.x: PM-JAY provides health cover of ₹5 lakh per poor family per year. PMUY concerns LPG connections, PM-KISAN provides farmer income support, and PM SVANidhi provides loans to street vendors.
6.tq: Separate similar welfare benefits by beneficiary group and benefit type.

6.s: The principal objective of Jal Jeevan Mission is to provide:
o: Pucca houses to every urban family
Property cards to all urban landowners
Tap water through functional household tap connections to every rural household
6.x: Jal Jeevan Mission aims to provide tap water through functional household tap connections to every rural household.
6.tq: Identify the service delivered by the mission rather than its ministry alone.

6.s:
Consider the following statements about JJM 2.0:
1. It is planned to continue up to December 2028.
2. Its outlay is ₹8.69 lakh crore.
3. Its target is 19.36 crore households.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: JJM 2.0 is planned up to December 2028, with an outlay of ₹8.69 lakh crore and a target of 19.36 crore households.
6.tq: Check the duration, financial outlay and physical target together.

6.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes PMAY-G from PMAY-U?
o: PMAY-G is implemented by MoHUA, whereas PMAY-U is implemented by Rural Development.
PMAY-G concerns LPG and PMAY-U concerns electricity connections.
PMAY-G is implemented by Rural Development, whereas PMAY-U is implemented by MoHUA.
Both are implemented by the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
6.x: PMAY-G is associated with the Ministry of Rural Development, while PMAY-U is associated with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs. Both concern pucca housing in rural and urban areas respectively.
6.tq: Compare the ministry and rural-urban scope instead of relying on similar abbreviations.

6.s: The assistance under PMAY-G is ₹1.20 lakh in plains and ₹1.30 lakh in hilly areas. Which amount is applicable to hilly areas?
6.x: PMAY-G provides ₹1.20 lakh in plains and ₹1.30 lakh in hilly areas.
6.tq: Use the geographical comparison to avoid reversing the two assistance amounts.

6.s: PMKVY primarily provides:
o: Tap water connections to rural households
6.x: The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana provides short-term skill training and certification and is associated with the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.
6.tq: Match the scheme with its precise operational objective.

6.s: PM Ujjwala Yojana is administered by the Ministry of:
6.x: PM Ujjwala Yojana is associated with the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and provides deposit-free LPG connections to adult women of poor households.
6.tq: Identify the correct ministry from the scheme’s commodity and beneficiary group.

6.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding PM Ujjwala Yojana?
1. It was launched in May 2016.
2. Ujjwala 2.0 was introduced in 2021.
3. It provides deposit-free LPG connections to adult women of poor households.
4. The number of connections mentioned for the scheme is 10.57 crore.
6.x: All four statements are correct. PMUY was launched in May 2016, Ujjwala 2.0 came in 2021, the beneficiaries are adult women of poor households, and 10.57 crore connections are recorded.
6.tq: Combine launch year, later version, beneficiary and numerical coverage in one verification.

6.s: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY is associated with which ministry and implementing institution?
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the National Health Authority
Ministry of Power and the National Skill Development Corporation
Ministry of Rural Development and SIDBI
Ministry of Jal Shakti and the Survey of India
6.x: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY is associated with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and is implemented through the National Health Authority.
6.tq: Match the scheme with its parent ministry and implementing institution.

6.s: SVAMITVA uses drone surveys primarily to provide:
o: Property cards for rural abadi land
6.x: SVAMITVA uses drone surveys conducted by the Survey of India to provide property cards for rural abadi land.
6.tq: Identify the instrument, land category and resulting document in the scheme.

6.s: Which scheme is correctly matched with its objective?
o: SVAMITVA — deposit-free LPG connection to adult women
PMKVY — ₹5 lakh health cover per poor family
PM-JAY — drone survey of rural abadi land
Saubhagya — electricity connection to every household
6.x: Saubhagya aims to provide electricity connections to every household. LPG connections, health cover and drone-based property cards are associated with PMUY, PM-JAY and SVAMITVA respectively.
6.tq: Find the correctly matched pair by separating the outputs of similar welfare schemes.

6.s: The target under SVAMITVA mentioned for rural villages is:
6.x: SVAMITVA has a target covering 6.62 lakh villages.
6.tq: Recall the precise physical target rather than confusing it with household targets under other schemes.

6.s:
Match the newer launch with the correct ministry:

a. PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana
b. Export Promotion Mission
c. RDI Scheme
d. Biopharma SHAKTI

i. Department of Science and Technology through the ANRF Board
ii. Department of Pharmaceuticals
iii. Agriculture
iv. Commerce and Industry

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
6.x: PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana belongs to Agriculture; the Export Promotion Mission to Commerce and Industry; the RDI Scheme to DST through the ANRF Board; and Biopharma SHAKTI to the Department of Pharmaceuticals.
6.tq: Start with the distinctive ministry for Biopharma SHAKTI and then complete the remaining pairs.

6.s: PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana is designed for:
o: 100 high-productivity districts for four years, benefiting 3.5 crore employees
100 low-productivity districts for six years, benefiting about 1.7 crore farmers
19.36 crore rural households for three years
6.x: PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana covers 100 low-productivity districts for six years and is expected to benefit about 1.7 crore farmers.
6.tq: Combine the district count, duration and beneficiary estimate to identify the scheme.

6.s: Under the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, 100% MSP procurement is specified for which group of pulses for four years?
6.x: The mission provides for 100% MSP procurement of tur, urad and masoor for four years, within the period 2025-26 to 2030-31.
6.tq: Distinguish the exact pulse trio from other agricultural commodities.

6.s: The approved corpus of the RDI Scheme is:
6.x: The RDI Scheme has a corpus of ₹1 lakh crore and was approved on 1 July 2025.
6.tq: Match the large corpus figure with the correct research and development scheme.

6.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Biopharma SHAKTI — ₹1 lakh crore corpus for six years
Export Promotion Mission — ₹25,060 crore for FY26–FY31
PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana — ₹10,000 crore for biologics
Mission Samriddh Gaon — 100% MSP procurement of pulses
6.x: The Export Promotion Mission has an allocation of ₹25,060 crore for FY26–FY31. Biopharma SHAKTI concerns ₹10,000 crore and biologics, PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana concerns employment, and Mission Samriddh Gaon concerns livelihood saturation.
6.tq: Use amount-period matching to detect swapped scheme features.

6.s: Biopharma SHAKTI has which of the following features?
o: ₹1 lakh crore corpus for research approved in July 2025
₹10,000 crore allocation for 2026–31 and development of 100 biologics by 2047
₹25,060 crore allocation for export promotion during FY26–FY31
₹99,446 crore allocation for 3.5 crore EPFO-linked jobs
6.x: Biopharma SHAKTI has an allocation of ₹10,000 crore for 2026–31 and aims at 100 biologics by 2047.
6.tq: Identify the scheme from its long-term target and sector-specific financial allocation.

6.s: PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana covers which period and employment target?
o: 1 August 2025 to 31 July 2027; 3.5 crore jobs through EPFO
1 July 2026 to 31 December 2028; 19.36 crore jobs through JJM
2026-31; 100 biologics through the Department of Pharmaceuticals
6.x: PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana covers 1 August 2025 to 31 July 2027 and aims to create 3.5 crore jobs through EPFO.
6.tq: Pair the scheme with its exact period, employment figure and institutional route.

6.s: Mission Samriddh Gaon is associated with:
o: A purpose-bound digital rupee food subsidy
Universal tap-water connections in every rural household
Livelihood saturation, initially piloted in two blocks of Madhya Pradesh
6.x: Mission Samriddh Gaon focuses on livelihood saturation and was initially piloted in two Madhya Pradesh blocks.
6.tq: Match the new mission with its objective and pilot location.

6.s: CBDC-based DBT under PM-GKAY uses purpose-bound e₹ primarily for:
6.x: The CBDC-based DBT arrangement under PM-GKAY uses purpose-bound digital rupees for food subsidy and is associated with Chandigarh and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
6.tq: Identify the purpose of the digital payment rather than the technology alone.

6.s:
With reference to the launch of major national programmes, consider the following pairs:

Programme — Date of launch
1. Make in India — 25 September 2014
2. Digital India — 1 July 2015
3. Startup India — 16 January 2016
4. SVAMITVA — 24 April 2020

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
6.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Make in India, Digital India, Startup India and SVAMITVA were launched on 25 September 2014, 1 July 2015, 16 January 2016 and 24 April 2020, respectively.
6.tq: Match each date with the programme before eliminating the coded options.

6.s: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015 by which institution?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
6.x: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015 by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. The programme is structured around nine pillars.
6.tq: Use the agency-purpose association to distinguish neighbouring technology departments.

6.s: SVAMITVA was launched on 24 April 2020 on the occasion of:
6.x: SVAMITVA was launched on 24 April 2020 on National Panchayati Raj Day.
6.tq: Link the launch date with the specific commemorative occasion.

6.s:
Arrange the following programmes in chronological order of their launch:
A. Make in India
B. Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan
C. Startup India
D. SVAMITVA
6.x: The correct sequence is Make in India (2014), Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan (2015), Startup India (2016) and SVAMITVA (2020).
6.tq: Fix the earliest and latest items first, then place the two intervening programmes.

6.s: The Gyan Bharatam Mission is primarily associated with:
6.x: The Gyan Bharatam Mission, announced in July 2025, focuses on manuscript digitisation. Its National Manuscript Survey began in March 2026.
6.tq: Identify the exact purpose instead of choosing a broadly related digitisation activity.

6.s: The AP cluster centre of the Gyan Bharatam Mission is run by:
6.x: The AP cluster centre of Gyan Bharatam is run by the Sanatana Jeevan Trust and deals particularly with palm-leaf manuscripts.
6.tq: Use the organisation-purpose association to identify the correct implementing institution.

6.s: Which of the following correctly describes Vibrant Villages Programme-I?
o: A Centrally Sponsored Scheme covering 46 blocks in 19 districts along the northern border
A Central Sector Scheme covering all international border villages from 2024–25 to 2028–29
A State-funded scheme covering coastal villages only
A scheme restricted to villages in the North-Eastern States
6.x: Vibrant Villages Programme-I is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme covering 46 blocks in 19 districts along the northern border, including areas in Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Ladakh.
6.tq: Separate the scheme’s classification, coverage and geography from those of its later version.

6.s: Vibrant Villages Programme-II covers villages on:
o: The coastline of the eastern States
The inter-State boundaries of the North-East
6.x: VVP-II, implemented from 2024–25 to 2028–29, covers villages on other international land borders. It is a Central Sector Scheme with 100% central funding.
6.tq: Discriminate between the northern-border focus of VVP-I and the other land borders under VVP-II.

6.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
6.x: VVP-I is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, whereas VVP-II is a Central Sector Scheme with 100% central funding. Therefore, VVP-I and 100% central funding are not correctly matched.
6.tq: Find the swapped feature between the two similarly named programmes.

6.s: The SPM Rurban Mission provides for population clusters of:
o: 25,000–50,000 in plains/coastal areas and 5,000–25,000 in desert, hilly and tribal areas
10,000–20,000 in plains and 20,000–40,000 in hilly areas
5,000–25,000 in plains/coastal areas and 25,000–50,000 in desert areas
6.x: The SPM Rurban Mission covers clusters of 25,000–50,000 people in plains and coastal areas, and 5,000–25,000 people in desert, hilly and tribal areas.
6.tq: Check the reversed population ranges and geographical conditions carefully.

6.s: The SPM Rurban Mission, launched in 2016, is funded mainly through:
o: A dedicated cess on rural property
6.x: The SPM Rurban Mission was launched in 2016 and is funded through convergence of different schemes. It envisages more than 300 clusters.
6.tq: Identify the funding mechanism rather than the numerical coverage.

6.s: Sampada, a platform for e-registration of property, is associated with which State?
6.x: Sampada is the Madhya Pradesh platform for e-registration of property.
6.tq: Pair the platform with its State rather than with a similarly named land-record service.

6.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Platform — Purpose
1. DigiLocker — Cloud-based storage of documents
2. e-Shram — National database of unorganised workers
3. e-Jagriti — Online consumer complaints
4. Mana Mitra — WhatsApp governance service in Andhra Pradesh
6.x: All four pairs are correct. DigiLocker provides cloud documents, e-Shram maintains the database of unorganised workers, e-Jagriti handles consumer complaints and Mana Mitra provides WhatsApp governance services in Andhra Pradesh.
6.tq: Start with the sure platform-purpose pairs and verify the State-specific service last.

6.s: DigiLocker documents are recognised as valid under:
o: The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, Rule 5
The Representation of the People Act, Section 9A
6.x: DigiLocker documents have legal validity under Rule 9A of the Information Technology Rules. DigiLocker was launched in 2015 by MeitY.
6.tq: Distinguish the exact rule number from similar statutory section numbers.

6.s: The e-Shram portal provides which of the following for unorganised workers?
6.x: e-Shram, launched in August 2021 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, creates a national database of unorganised workers and provides a 12-digit UAN.
6.tq: Use the number-format clue to distinguish the worker database identifier from other government numbers.

6.s: Sujal Gaon ID under Sujalam Bharat is intended to provide:
o: A land title number for rural properties
A digital identity for each rural water supply scheme
A digital identity for every urban household
A subsidy code for LPG consumers
6.x: Sujal Gaon ID provides a digital identity for each rural water scheme under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. It is associated with the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
6.tq: Infer the service from the rural-water context and reject unrelated identity systems.

6.s: PM-AJAY Portal and AJAY app are associated with which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
6.x: The PM-AJAY Portal and AJAY app are associated with the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and aim to make PM-AJAY paperless.
6.tq: Apply the ‘which Ministry’ trap to distinguish closely related welfare departments.

6.s:
Consider the following statements about PM-SETU for ITI upgradation:
1. Its total outlay is ₹60,000 crore over five years.
2. The Centre, States and industry contribute ₹30,000 crore, ₹20,000 crore and ₹10,000 crore respectively.
3. The World Bank and ADB co-finance 50% of the central share.
4. It covers 1,000 ITIs in hub-and-spoke clusters.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: All four statements are correct. PM-SETU has a ₹60,000 crore five-year outlay, the stated Centre-State-industry sharing pattern, multilateral co-financing of half the central share and coverage of 1,000 ITIs.
6.tq: Break the scheme into outlay, contribution, external partner and coverage before choosing the code.

6.s: Which of the following schemes is identified as World Bank-aided and intended for minority youth?
6.x: Nai Manzil is a World Bank-aided programme intended for minority youth. Atal Bhujal Yojana is also listed among World Bank-aided schemes, but has a different focus.
6.tq: Separate schemes sharing the same external partner by their target group and purpose.

6.s: The revised outlay for PM-KISAN up to 2030–31 is:
6.x: PM-KISAN has been extended up to 2030–31 with an outlay of ₹3.15 lakh crore.
6.tq: Read the lakh-crore figure precisely and eliminate options differing by one digit.

6.s: SASCI provides States with:
o: Foreign exchange loans for private infrastructure projects
Ten-year interest-bearing revenue loans within the 3% deficit cap
50-year interest-free capital expenditure loans outside the 3% deficit cap
6.x: SASCI provides 50-year interest-free loans to States for capital expenditure. These loans are outside the 3% fiscal deficit cap.
6.tq: Identify both the purpose and the exceptional fiscal treatment in the applied description.

6.s: ULLAS, also known as Nav Bharat Saksharta, primarily targets:
o: Adult literacy among persons aged 15 years and above
Digital literacy among children below six years
6.x: ULLAS is the adult literacy programme for persons aged 15 years and above, with the slogan ‘Jan Jan Sakshar’. Its outlay is ₹1,037.90 crore for 2022–27.
6.tq: Match the programme with its age group and educational objective.

6.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: PM SHRI — Collateral-free higher education loans
DIKSHA — Digital content for school teaching
6.x: PM SHRI is a programme for developing more than 14,500 model schools aligned with NEP. Collateral-free education loans are associated with PM Vidyalaxmi.
6.tq: Find the purpose swapped between two education schemes.

6.s: The National Skills Qualifications Framework is primarily concerned with:
o: Providing direct cash transfers to trainees
6.x: NSQF establishes competency-based qualification levels. Care-giver training is also aligned with the framework.
6.tq: Choose the definition that states what the framework measures rather than an associated activity.

6.s: PM SHRI schools are intended to be:
o: Residential schools exclusively for tribal children
More than 14,500 model schools aligned with NEP
6.x: PM SHRI aims to develop more than 14,500 model schools aligned with the National Education Policy. The implementation period is 2022–23 to 2026–27.
6.tq: Use the scale and model-school objective to distinguish PM SHRI from other education initiatives.

6.s: PM Vidyalaxmi, launched in November 2024, provides:
6.x: PM Vidyalaxmi provides collateral-free education loans. The number of covered institutions has subsequently reached 1,425.
6.tq: Distinguish student-finance support from school-improvement and State-capital schemes.

6.s: Which of the following was the first Union Territory to become fully literate under ULLAS?
6.x: Ladakh became the first Union Territory to become fully literate under ULLAS in 2024. The benchmark for being declared fully literate is 95% literacy.
6.tq: Separate the first Union Territory from the first State in the ULLAS sequence.

6.s: The literacy threshold used for declaring an area fully literate under ULLAS is:
6.x: The benchmark for being declared fully literate under ULLAS is 95% literacy; complete 100% literacy is not required.
6.tq: Reject the attractive but excessive ‘100 percent’ threshold.

6.s: Under PAHAL, the LPG subsidy is transferred when:
o: The subsidy is credited to the gas agency before delivery
The consumer pays a subsidised price and receives no subsequent transfer
The consumer receives the cylinder free of cost from the distributor
The consumer buys the cylinder at market price and the subsidy is credited to the Aadhaar-seeded bank account
6.x: Under PAHAL, the LPG cylinder is bought at market price and the subsidy is subsequently credited to the consumer’s Aadhaar-seeded bank account.
6.tq: Trace the sequence of purchase, subsidy credit and bank-account linkage.

6.s: The JAM trinity, which forms the base of Direct Benefit Transfer, consists of:
6.x: JAM stands for Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile. The idea was set out in the Economic Survey 2014–15 and became the foundation for DBT delivery.
6.tq: Expand the acronym exactly and avoid replacing one of its three components with a policy objective.

6.s: CBDC-based DBT involves payment of subsidy through:
6.x: Under CBDC-based DBT, the subsidy is paid as a programmable digital rupee. This mechanism was introduced in 2026.
6.tq: Identify the payment instrument and distinguish it from conventional bank-account DBT.

6.s: Which scheme replaced the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) with effect from 1 July 2026?
6.x: The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 replaced MGNREGA with effect from 1 July 2026.
6.tq: Use direct old-name to new-name recall.

6.s: The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 was passed in which month and year?
6.x: The Act was passed in December 2025 and came into force on 1 July 2026.
6.tq: Separate the date of enactment from the date of commencement.

6.s:
With reference to the VB-G RAM G Act, consider the following statements:
1. It provides for 125 days of employment.
2. Wages are indexed to the Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers.
3. It came into force on 1 July 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: All three statements are correct: the Act provides 125 days of employment, indexes wages to CPI-AL, and came into force on 1 July 2026.
6.tq: Check each numerical and date statement independently before selecting the complete combination.

6.s: Which of the following is a feature associated with the VB-G RAM G Act as reported in current debates?
o: A complete exemption from biometric verification
6.x: The Act permits a 60-day farm-season blackout. The other alternatives do not represent the stated features.
6.tq: Identify the specific criticism rather than accepting absolute or reversed claims.

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding criticisms of the VB-G RAM G framework:
1. Biometric checks may exclude some workers.
2. States bear a 40% share of wages.
3. The framework completely removes the role of technology in worker verification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: Biometric checks may exclude workers and States bear a 40% wage share. Statement 3 is false because biometric checks are part of the framework.
6.tq: Find the reversed statement among otherwise related policy features.

6.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Earlier scheme)
a. Swadhar Greh and Ujjwala
b. Working Women Hostel
c. National Creche

d. Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan

List-II (Present status/name)
i. Palna
ii. MY Bharat (IYB)
iii. Shakti Sadan
iv. Sakhi Niwas
6.x: Swadhar Greh and Ujjwala were merged as Shakti Sadan; Working Women Hostel became Sakhi Niwas; National Creche became Palna; and Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan became MY Bharat (IYB).
6.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with mismatched renamed schemes.

6.s: Swadhar Greh and Ujjwala were merged into which scheme under Mission Shakti–Samarthya?
6.x: Swadhar Greh and Ujjwala, both associated with anti-trafficking support, were merged into Shakti Sadan under Mission Shakti–Samarthya.
6.tq: Distinguish the merged scheme from similarly renamed welfare schemes.

6.s: Working Women Hostel and National Creche were renamed, respectively, as:
6.x: Working Women Hostel was renamed Sakhi Niwas, while National Creche was renamed Palna.
6.tq: Test the order of two closely related renamed schemes.

6.s: Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan is associated with which new identity?
6.x: Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan was associated with MY Bharat (IYB).
6.tq: Use direct organisation-to-new-identity matching.

6.s: Which one of the following scheme-status pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: PM SVANidhi — Restructured in 2025 and extended to March 2030
Jal Jeevan Mission — Extended to December 2028
6.x: DILRMP is associated with the DILRMP 3.0 guidelines issued on 12 September 2026, not an extension to March 2030. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
6.tq: Find the wrong status by comparing the exact extension or guideline detail.

6.s: The PM SVANidhi scheme was restructured in 2025 and extended up to:
6.x: PM SVANidhi was restructured in 2025 and extended up to March 2030.
6.tq: Distinguish the extension year from the nearby scheme-extension dates.

6.s: The Jal Jeevan Mission has been extended up to:
6.x: The Jal Jeevan Mission was extended up to December 2028.
6.tq: Recall the precise month-year endpoint rather than only the year.

6.s:
With reference to IVFRT, consider the following statements:
1. IVFRT is associated with the Ministry of Home Affairs.
2. It has been extended up to March 2031.
3. Its extension was reported in April 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: IVFRT is associated with the Ministry of Home Affairs, was extended to March 2031, and the extension was reported in April 2026.
6.tq: Combine ministry, endpoint and reporting-date facts without reversing their relationships.

6.s: DILRMP 3.0 guidelines were issued on:
6.x: The DILRMP 3.0 guidelines were issued on 12 September 2026.
6.tq: Use exact-date discrimination among closely spaced current-affairs dates.

6.s: Which State received ₹2,545.50 crore under VB-G RAM G?
6.x: Andhra Pradesh received ₹2,545.50 crore under VB-G RAM G.
6.tq: Link the exact financial figure to the correct State.

6.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh in the context of the schemes and programmes mentioned:
1. Andhra Pradesh is a PURVODAYA State.
2. It has 359 Rurban panchayats.
3. It ranked second under MISHTI.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
6.x: All three statements are correct: Andhra Pradesh is a PURVODAYA State, has 359 Rurban panchayats, and ranked second under MISHTI.
6.tq: Treat each State-specific current-affairs fact as an independent statement.

6.s: Under Deepam-2, eligible beneficiaries in Andhra Pradesh receive how many free LPG cylinders a year alongside PMUY?
6.x: Deepam-2 provides three free LPG cylinders a year alongside the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana.
6.tq: Test the exact benefit count in a welfare scheme.

6.s: PM-KISAN payments in NTR district were reported to be ₹494.75 crore. This district is in:
6.x: NTR district is in Andhra Pradesh, where PM-KISAN payments of ₹494.75 crore were reported.
6.tq: Connect the district-specific figure with its State rather than confusing it with a national total.

6.s: The extension of PM-KISAN referred to in the current policy context is up to:
6.x: PM-KISAN was extended up to 2030–31.
6.tq: Distinguish the scheme’s extension period from other March-end deadlines.

6.s: Which of the following correctly describes the position of Andhra Pradesh under the PURVODAYA initiative?
o: It is excluded from the PURVODAYA States.
It is identified as a PURVODAYA State.
It is identified only as a MISHTI State and not as a PURVODAYA State.
It is included only under DILRMP 3.0.
6.x: Andhra Pradesh is identified as a PURVODAYA State.
6.tq: Apply the State-specific classification directly to the given policy context.

6.s: The Comptroller and Auditor General identified which issue in relation to the Green India Mission?
o: Poor convergence with CAMPA and MGNREGS
Complete transfer of the mission to local bodies
Excessive convergence with CAMPA and MGNREGS
6.x: The CAG found gaps in the Green India Mission, particularly poor convergence with CAMPA and MGNREGS.
6.tq: Watch for the reversed comparison trap in a criticism-based question.

6.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: MISHTI — Andhra Pradesh’s LPG distribution scheme
6.x: Mizoram was identified as the first fully literate State. Bharat Taxi is the first cooperative ride-hailing platform, while the other two descriptions are incorrect.
6.tq: Separate the correct identity from nearby but reversed programme descriptions.

6.s: Bharat Taxi is described as India’s first:
6.x: Bharat Taxi is described as the first cooperative ride-hailing platform.
6.tq: Recall the distinctive first associated with the platform.

6.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. VB-G RAM G Act comes into force
B. VB-G RAM G Act is passed
C. PM SVANidhi is restructured
D. DILRMP 3.0 guidelines are issued
6.x: The Act was passed in December 2025, PM SVANidhi was restructured in 2025, the Act came into force on 1 July 2026, and DILRMP 3.0 guidelines were issued on 12 September 2026. Within the year 2025, the stated sequence places passage before the restructuring in the intended chronology.
6.tq: Use the first and last events, then resolve the middle dates carefully.

7.s: The Panel constituted in 2019 for selling 149 State-owned oil and gas fields was chaired by whom?
7.x: The panel for selling 149 State-owned oil and gas fields was chaired by Rajiv Kumar.
7.tq: Direct chairperson identification using nearby committee names as distractors.

7.s: The High-Level Committee on simultaneous elections constituted in 2023–24 was chaired by:
7.x: The High-Level Committee on simultaneous elections, or One Nation One Election, was chaired by Ram Nath Kovind.
7.tq: Direct chairperson recall with a subject-based committee trap.

7.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. National Commission on Farmers — M.S. Swaminathan
2. Committee on MSP and crop diversification — Sanjay Agrawal
3. NCRWC — M.N. Venkatachaliah
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
7.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. The National Commission on Farmers was chaired by M.S. Swaminathan, the MSP and crop-diversification committee by Sanjay Agrawal, and the NCRWC by M.N. Venkatachaliah.
7.tq: Statement matching based on chairperson–committee associations.

7.s: The National Commission on Farmers recommended that the Minimum Support Price should be fixed at:
7.x: The National Commission on Farmers, chaired by M.S. Swaminathan, recommended MSP at C2 cost plus 50 percent.
7.tq: Precise numerical and terminology discrimination between cost concepts.

7.s: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC), constituted in 2002, proposed the establishment of a:
o: National Commission for Higher Education and Research
7.x: The NCRWC, chaired by M.N. Venkatachaliah, proposed a National Judicial Commission.
7.tq: Direct proposal identification with similarly named constitutional bodies as distractors.

7.s: The High-Level Committee on Demographic Change, proposed in May 2026, was chaired by:
7.x: The High-Level Committee on Demographic Change was chaired by Justice Prakash Prabhakar Navlekar and dealt with demographic change arising from illegal immigration.
7.tq: Chairperson–terms of reference discrimination among recent committees.

7.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: K. Kasturirangan — Draft National Education Policy
Vijay Kelkar — Revisiting and revitalising the PPP model
7.x: M. Narasimham chaired committees on banking-sector reforms. Electoral reforms were associated with the Dinesh Goswami and Indrajit Gupta committees.
7.tq: Find the wrong person–subject association.

7.s: The Urjit Patel Committee was associated with which of the following subjects?
7.x: The Urjit Patel Committee dealt with inflation targeting and recommended a target of 4 percent with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2 percent.
7.tq: One-fact subject recall with related committee subjects as distractors.

7.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee)
A. Nachiket Mor
B. Shanta Kumar
C. Ashok Dalwai
D. Santhanam

List-II (Subject)
I. Prevention of corruption
II. Doubling farmers’ income
III. Financial inclusion
IV. FCI–PDS reform

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
7.x: Nachiket Mor was associated with financial inclusion, Shanta Kumar with FCI–PDS reform, Ashok Dalwai with doubling farmers’ income, and Santhanam with prevention of corruption.
7.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes in a committee–subject match.

7.s: The Santhanam Committee of 1962–63 is associated with which significant institutional development?
7.x: The Santhanam Committee dealt with prevention of corruption and led to the establishment of the CBI.
7.tq: Institutional outcome recall from a committee report.

7.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. NMP 1.0 was launched in 2021.
2. NMP 2.0 covers FY 2026–30.
3. NMP 2.0 envisages ₹16.72 lakh crore through asset monetisation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: All three statements are correct. NMP 1.0 was launched in 2021, while NMP 2.0 covers FY 2026–30 and targets ₹16.72 lakh crore.
7.tq: Combine date, period and monetary figure in a coded statement question.

7.s: NMP 2.0 envisages private investment of approximately:
7.x: NMP 2.0 envisages private investment of ₹5.8 lakh crore within the overall asset-monetisation target of ₹16.72 lakh crore.
7.tq: Distinguish the overall target from the private-investment component.

7.s: Which institution prepared the National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0?
o: Core Group of Secretaries on Asset Monetisation
7.x: NMP 2.0 was prepared by NITI Aayog. Its implementation is monitored by the Core Group of Secretaries on Asset Monetisation.
7.tq: Separate the preparing agency from the monitoring mechanism.

7.s: The Core Group of Secretaries on Asset Monetisation is chaired by the:
o: Secretary, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
7.x: The Core Group of Secretaries on Asset Monetisation is chaired by the Cabinet Secretary.
7.tq: Authority-based question asking who performs the monitoring role.

7.s: The Nandan Nilekani task force announced in 2025–26 relates to:
o: Reforming the National Testing Agency through leak-proof, technology-driven examinations
7.x: The Nandan Nilekani task force was set up after the NEET-UG 2026 leak to develop leak-proof, technology-driven examinations.
7.tq: Identify the institutional response from the problem described in the scenario.

7.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Justice R. Subhash Reddy panel — Gorkha issue
Pankaj Kumar Singh Committee — NEET examination technology
High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat — electoral reforms
7.x: The K. Radhakrishnan Committee was associated with reform of the National Testing Agency. The Justice R. Subhash Reddy panel dealt with police action in the NEET protests, and the Pankaj Kumar Singh committee with the Gorkha issue.
7.tq: Pair discrimination using swapped committee subjects.

7.s: The 16th Finance Commission was constituted on:
7.x: The 16th Finance Commission was constituted on 31 December 2023.
7.tq: Date discrimination among constitution and award-period dates.

7.s: Who is the Chairperson of the 16th Finance Commission?
7.x: Dr Arvind Panagariya is the Chairperson of the 16th Finance Commission.
7.tq: Direct chairperson recall from a commission composition list.

7.s: Which one of the following is NOT a member listed for the 16th Finance Commission?
7.x: T. Rabi Sankar, Annie George Mathew and Manoj Panda are listed members of the 16th Finance Commission. Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai chairs the 8th Central Pay Commission.
7.tq: Find the outsider in a composition-based question.

7.s: The award period of the 16th Finance Commission is:
7.x: The 16th Finance Commission’s award period is from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031.
7.tq: Distinguish the award period from the commission’s constitution date.

7.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 16th Finance Commission:
1. It is a constitutional commission under Article 280.
2. It retained vertical devolution at 41 percent.
3. It assigned a 10 percent weight to contribution to GDP.
4. It provided ₹4.35 lakh crore to gram panchayats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: All four statements are correct. The 16th Finance Commission functions under Article 280, retained 41 percent vertical devolution, included a 10 percent GDP-contribution criterion and provided ₹4.35 lakh crore to gram panchayats.
7.tq: Multi-parameter statement testing with constitutional, percentage and monetary facts.

7.s: The 8th Central Pay Commission is chaired by:
7.x: Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai chairs the 8th Central Pay Commission.
7.tq: Direct chairperson recall with judicial names as close distractors.

7.s: The terms of reference of the 8th Central Pay Commission include:
o: Parliamentary seat delimitation and women’s reservation
Only salaries of Union civil servants
7.x: The 8th Central Pay Commission deals with pay, allowances and pensions. Its report is to be submitted in 18 months and is effective from 1 January 2026.
7.tq: Avoid the restrictive-word trap in a terms-of-reference question.

7.s: The proposed Delimitation Commission under the Delimitation Bill, 2026 is to be headed by:
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
7.x: The proposed Delimitation Commission is to be headed by a Supreme Court judge and is intended to redraw seats under the Delimitation Bill, 2026.
7.tq: Who-would-do-this-job authority identification.

7.s: The National Tribunals Commission proposed under the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026 deals primarily with:
o: Appointment of members of the Finance Commission
7.x: The National Tribunals Commission is proposed to deal with tribunal appointments, reviews and discipline.
7.tq: Match the body’s proposed functions with the institutional situation.

7.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Tribunals Commission:
1. It is proposed to have five members.
2. Its headquarters will be in New Delhi.
3. It is to be headed by a former Supreme Court judge or a High Court Chief Justice.
4. The Bill was moved by Arjun Ram Meghwal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: All four statements are correct. The proposed Commission has five members, headquarters at New Delhi, a head drawn from former Supreme Court judges or High Court Chief Justices, and the Bill was moved by Arjun Ram Meghwal.
7.tq: Composition, location, authority and legislative-detail combination.

7.s: Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan is proposed as a single apex body replacing:
7.x: The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan is proposed as a single apex higher-education regulator replacing the UGC, AICTE and NCTE.
7.tq: Regulator-composition discrimination using statutory bodies as distractors.

7.s: The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025 was introduced in the Lok Sabha in:
7.x: The VBSA Bill, 2025 was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2025.
7.tq: Chronological date recall using nearby legislative dates as distractors.

7.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025 is correct?
o: It proposed separate apex regulators for UGC, AICTE and NCTE.
It was passed in the Monsoon Session of 2026 without referral to a committee.
It was sent to a Joint Parliamentary Committee, which flagged centralisation.
It excluded State universities from its operation without any modification.
7.x: The Bill was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee, which flagged concerns about centralisation. After objections from Andhra Pradesh, the Centre agreed that State consent would be required for decisions concerning colleges of State universities, and the Bill was not passed in the Monsoon Session of 2026.
7.tq: Identify the precise legislative-status statement among altered details.

7.s: The National Commission for Higher Education and Research (NCHER) was proposed after the recommendations of the:
7.x: NCHER was proposed after the Yashpal Committee of 2009. It was announced by HRD Minister Kapil Sibal but was never enacted.
7.tq: Committee-to-proposal linkage with closely related education committees as traps.

7.s: Who announced the proposal for the National Commission for Higher Education and Research?
7.x: The NCHER proposal was announced by the then HRD Minister Kapil Sibal.
7.tq: Minister–proposal association recall.

7.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 sought to increase the total Lok Sabha seats from 543 to:
7.x: The Bill proposed increasing Lok Sabha seats from 543 to 850, comprising 815 seats for States and 35 for Union Territories.
7.tq: Separate the total from its State and Union Territory components.

7.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026:
1. It proposed amendments to Articles 81, 82 and 334A.
2. It sought early delimitation and women’s quota.
3. It was defeated in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026.
4. It secured the required two-thirds majority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Bill was defeated on 17 April 2026 because it lacked the required two-thirds majority; therefore statement 4 is false.
7.tq: Find the single reversed legislative-outcome statement.

7.s:
Arrange the following bodies or proposals in chronological order of their relevant year:
A. NCHER proposal after the Yashpal Committee
B. NITI Aayog
C. NMP 1.0
D. VBSA Bill

Select the correct sequence.
7.x: The sequence is A (2009), B (2015), C (2021) and D (2025).
7.tq: Use the first and last dates, then place the intermediate milestones.

7.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the status of the body?
7.x: The NCBC became a constitutional body under Article 338B through the 102nd Amendment, 2018. NCSC is constitutional, NHRC is statutory and NITI Aayog is neither constitutional nor statutory.
7.tq: Compare constitutional, statutory and non-statutory classifications.

7.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes derives its constitutional status from:
7.x: NCST is provided under Article 338A. Article 338 relates to NCSC, Article 338B to NCBC and Article 280 to the Finance Commission.
7.tq: Discriminate among adjacent constitutional Articles.

7.s: Which of the following bodies is classified as neither constitutional nor statutory?
7.x: NITI Aayog is classified as neither constitutional nor statutory. The CBI is based on the DSPE Act, while NHRC and NCM are statutory bodies.
7.tq: Odd-one-out classification based on legal status.

7.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. NCBC was statutory when established in 1993.
2. NCBC became constitutional through the 102nd Amendment Act, 2018.
3. NCSC and NCST were separated through the 89th Amendment of 2003.
4. NHRC was established in 1992.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. NHRC was established in 1993, not 1992; therefore statement 4 is false. NCW and NCM are associated with 1992 and the NCM Act respectively.
7.tq: Date and legal-status discrimination within a comparison table.

7.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: NCSC — Statutory body under the 1993 Act
NCM — Statutory body under the 1992 Act
NCISM and NCH — Statutory bodies under the 2020 Acts
7.x: NCSC is a constitutional body under Article 338, not a statutory body under the 1993 Act. NCISM and NCH are statutory under the 2020 Acts, while NCW and NCM are statutory bodies.
7.tq: Spot the wrong legal-status classification.

7.s: The report of the 16th Finance Commission was tabled in the Lok Sabha on:
7.x: The 16th Finance Commission report was tabled in the Lok Sabha on 1 February 2026.
7.tq: Use precise date discrimination among closely related dates.

7.s: Which one of the following recommendations of the 16th Finance Commission was accepted by the Centre for 2026–27?
7.x: The Centre accepted the 16th Finance Commission’s recommendation of retaining the States’ vertical devolution share at 41%.
7.tq: Test the exact percentage while using nearby percentages as distractors.

7.s: The Finance Commission grants provided by the Centre for 2026–27 amounted to:
7.x: The Centre provided ₹1.4 lakh crore in Finance Commission grants for 2026–27.
7.tq: Distinguish decimal placement and magnitude in a numerical fact.

7.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Joint Parliamentary Committee on simultaneous elections:
1. Its term was extended to the last week of the Monsoon Session of 2026.
2. Former Chief Justices of India told the panel that the Bill does not violate the Basic Structure.
3. Its report had already been accepted by the Centre by March 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the committee was still pending and its term had been extended.
7.tq: Find the wrong status statement by separating pending developments from completed actions.

7.s: Which States objected to the centralising provisions of the JPC on the VBSA Bill?
o: Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh
Andhra Pradesh, Meghalaya and Madhya Pradesh
7.x: Andhra Pradesh, Meghalaya and Madhya Pradesh objected to the centralising provisions of the VBSA Bill.
7.tq: Test membership of a specific group using neighbouring State substitutions.

7.s: The 393rd Report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture is titled:
7.x: The 393rd Report is titled “From Manuscript to Mission” and deals with manuscripts and artificial intelligence.
7.tq: Use the exact official title rather than a familiar-sounding paraphrase.

7.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Kasturirangan Committee — National Education Policy, 2020
2. Urjit Patel Committee — 2016 amendment to the RBI Act
3. 59th and 114th Law Commission Reports — Became laws
4. 255th Law Commission Report — Totalisers, with the matter pending before the Supreme Court
7.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The Kasturirangan recommendations became associated with NEP 2020, the Urjit Patel recommendation with the 2016 RBI Act amendment, the 59th and 114th reports became laws, and the 255th report on totalisers remained pending.
7.tq: Start from sure pairs and verify whether the status is accepted or pending.

7.s: Which of the following matters was specifically listed as pending?
o: The addition of heatwaves as a notified disaster
7.x: The All India Judicial Service was listed among the pending matters. The other matters had been accepted or enacted.
7.tq: Find the one item belonging to the pending category.

7.s: Which one of the following is a constitutional and quasi-judicial body established under Article 280?
7.x: The Finance Commission is a constitutional, quasi-judicial body under Article 280.
7.tq: Match the body with its constitutional basis and institutional nature.

7.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The NCSC is provided for under Article 338.
2. The NCST is provided for under Article 338A.
3. Both bodies acquired their present constitutional basis through the 89th Constitutional Amendment of 2003.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: All three statements are correct. The NCSC is associated with Article 338, the NCST with Article 338A, and their separation followed the 89th Amendment of 2003.
7.tq: Combine article-number and amendment-number facts in a coded statement question.

7.s: The National Commission for Minorities is a:
o: Non-statutory advisory body under the Department of Expenditure
Statutory body under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992
Society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860
7.x: The National Commission for Minorities is a statutory body created under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
7.tq: Discriminate between constitutional, statutory, non-statutory and society status.

7.s: Who was appointed Chair of the National Commission for Minorities in July 2026?
7.x: Harjit Singh Grewal was the chair of the National Commission for Minorities in July 2026.
7.tq: Use a chairperson-versus-chairperson confusable-pair question.

7.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pay Commission — Constitutional body under Article 280
NHRC — Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
7.x: The Pay Commission is not a constitutional body; it is a non-statutory, advisory body associated with the Department of Expenditure. The other pairs are correctly matched.
7.tq: Identify the wrong institutional classification rather than the wrong legal reference.

7.s: Linguistic minorities are protected through which constitutional provision and institutional arrangement?
o: Article 350B and a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
7.x: Linguistic minorities do not fall under the National Commission for Minorities. They are dealt with by a Special Officer under Article 350B.
7.tq: Separate linguistic minorities from the jurisdiction of the National Commission for Minorities.

7.s:
With reference to the National Testing Agency, consider the following statements:
1. It is only a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
2. A petition after the 2026 NEET leak sought to make it a statutory body.
3. It is a constitutional body established under Article 280.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the NTA is not a constitutional body under Article 280; it is a society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
7.tq: Use the statutory-versus-society distinction to reject an incorrect constitutional classification.

7.s: Which criterion received the highest weight under the 16th Finance Commission’s award for 2026–31?
7.x: Income distance received the highest weight under the 16th Finance Commission, at 42.5%.
7.tq: Compare the largest weights rather than relying on the presence of a new criterion.

7.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the weights assigned to income distance by the 15th and 16th Finance Commissions?
7.x: The weight for income distance declined from 45% under the 15th Finance Commission to 42.5% under the 16th Finance Commission.
7.tq: Read the comparison table horizontally and preserve the order of the commissions.

7.s: Under the 16th Finance Commission, the weight assigned to population based on the 2011 Census is:
7.x: Population based on the 2011 Census received a weight of 17.5% under the 16th Finance Commission, compared with 15% under the 15th Finance Commission.
7.tq: Test an exact table value using closely spaced percentage options.

7.s: Which criterion was introduced by the 16th Finance Commission with a weight of 10% but was absent in the 15th Finance Commission’s criteria?
7.x: Contribution to GDP was introduced as a new criterion by the 16th Finance Commission with a weight of 10%.
7.tq: Identify the new row in a comparison table.

7.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Finance Commission criteria:
1. The weight for area declined from 15% under the 15th Finance Commission to 10% under the 16th Finance Commission.
2. The weight for forest and ecology remained at 10% under both Commissions.
3. Tax and fiscal effort was dropped by the 16th Finance Commission.
4. Demographic performance was reduced from 12.5% to 10%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: All four statements are correct. Area and demographic performance received lower weights, forest and ecology remained unchanged, and tax and fiscal effort was dropped.
7.tq: Check every row of a comparison table before selecting the coded combination.

7.s: Under the 16th Finance Commission, demographic performance is measured by:
o: The absolute population of a State in 2011
7.x: The 16th Finance Commission measures demographic performance by population growth during 1971–2011.
7.tq: Distinguish the specified time span from nearby census periods.

7.s: A State’s open forests are included under which Finance Commission criterion under the 16th Finance Commission?
7.x: The forest and ecology criterion under the 16th Finance Commission includes open forests as well.
7.tq: Apply a descriptive change to the correct criterion rather than to a neighbouring criterion.

7.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 16th Finance Commission’s grants:
1. The total grants amounted to ₹9.47 lakh crore.
2. Revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants were discontinued.
3. The vertical devolution share excluded cesses and surcharges.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: All three statements are correct. The grants totalled ₹9.47 lakh crore, the specified categories were discontinued, and the 41% vertical share excluded cesses and surcharges.
7.tq: Combine a numerical fact with policy changes and an exclusion clause.

7.s: The corpus of the SDRF and SDMF recommended under the 16th Finance Commission is:
7.x: The combined SDRF and SDMF corpus was recommended at ₹2,04,401 crore.
7.tq: Test the exact figure while varying digit order and place value.

7.s: The SDRF/SDMF corpus is to be shared in which manner for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and for other States, respectively?
7.x: The sharing pattern is 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and 75:25 for other States.
7.tq: Preserve the order of the two categories while comparing ratios.

7.s: Which of the following was recommended as a notified disaster on the advice of the 16th Finance Commission?
7.x: Heatwaves and lightning were added as notified disasters on the advice of the 16th Finance Commission.
7.tq: Select the newly added pair rather than established disaster categories.

7.s: Urban local governments were allocated what amount under the 16th Finance Commission, representing what share of local-body grants?
7.x: Urban local governments were allocated ₹3.5 lakh crore, equal to 45% of local-body grants. Under the 15th Finance Commission, the corresponding share was 36%.
7.tq: Link the amount and percentage in a two-part quantitative question.

7.s: The urbanisation premium recommended by the 16th Finance Commission amounted to:
7.x: The 16th Finance Commission recommended an urbanisation premium of ₹10,000 crore.
7.tq: Use exact amount recognition with scale-based distractors.

7.s: The RBI Q-SAFE Committee examined:
o: Assured payouts under the National Pension System
Investment rules under the National Pension System
7.x: The RBI Q-SAFE Committee examined quantum-safe financial infrastructure.
7.tq: Match the committee acronym and institution with the issue examined.

7.s: Who chaired the RBI Q-SAFE Committee?
7.x: The eight-member RBI Q-SAFE Committee was chaired by Prof. Anil Prabhakar of IIT Madras.
7.tq: Use chairperson discrimination among expert-group names.

7.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. SEBI High-Level Committee — Pratyush Sinha — Conflict of interest in SEBI
2. PFRDA Committee — M.S. Sahoo — Assured payouts under NPS
3. PFRDA Committee — Narayan Ramachandran — NPS investment rules
7.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Pratyush Sinha chaired the SEBI committee on conflict of interest, M.S. Sahoo examined assured NPS payouts, and Narayan Ramachandran examined NPS investment rules.
7.tq: Start with the sure chair–issue pair and verify all remaining matches.

7.s: The framework recommended by the SEBI High-Level Committee on conflict of interest in SEBI was approved in:
7.x: The framework on conflict of interest in SEBI was approved in March 2026.
7.tq: Distinguish the approval date from dates associated with other current-affairs developments.

7.s: The 121st Report of the Law Commission of India dealt with which of the following subjects?
7.x: The 121st Report, published in 1987, dealt with the National Judicial Service Commission.
7.tq: Match the report number with its precise subject.

7.s: The 170th Report of the Law Commission of India recommended which of the following electoral reforms?
o: Increasing Lok Sabha strength by 25 per cent through a party-list system
Simultaneous elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
De-registration of parties that do not contest elections for ten years
7.x: The 170th Report, submitted in 1999, recommended raising the strength of the Lok Sabha by 25 per cent through a party-list arrangement.
7.tq: Use the distinctive recommendation to identify the report.

7.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: 214th Report — Review of the procedure for appointing judges
279th Report — Draft model Bilateral Investment Treaty
