7.x: The 214th Report, submitted in 2008, reviewed the procedure for appointing judges. The other subjects belong to different reports or are not stated for those report numbers.
7.tq: Start from the sure report–subject pair and eliminate swapped subjects.

7.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. 14th Report — Reform of judicial administration
b. 59th Report — Family courts
c. 114th Report — Gram Nyayalayas
d. 230th Report — “Uncle judge” syndrome in High Courts
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
7.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The 14th, 59th, 114th and 230th Reports dealt respectively with judicial administration, family courts, Gram Nyayalayas and the “Uncle judge” syndrome.
7.tq: Check each report–subject pair independently before selecting the coded combination.

7.s: The 255th Report of the Law Commission of India, submitted in 2015, recommended which of the following?
o: A constitutional amendment establishing a National Judicial Service Commission
A single regulator for higher education
EVM totalisers and de-registration of parties that skip elections for ten years
7.x: The 255th Report dealt with electoral reforms, including EVM totalisers and de-registration of parties that do not contest elections for ten years.
7.tq: Identify the report through its paired electoral-reform recommendations.

7.s: The 279th Report of the Law Commission recommended that sedition should be:
o: Applied only during a national emergency
7.x: The 279th Report, submitted in 2023, recommended retaining sedition with safeguards.
7.tq: Distinguish retention with safeguards from complete repeal or unrestricted use.

7.s: What was the position taken in the 2018 Consultation Paper of the 21st Law Commission on a Uniform Civil Code?
o: It was neither necessary nor desirable at that stage
It was desirable only for personal laws of minorities
It was constitutionally compulsory and immediately implementable
It was declared outside the scope of the Law Commission
7.x: The 2018 Consultation Paper stated that a Uniform Civil Code was “neither necessary nor desirable at this stage.”
7.tq: Test the exact official formulation rather than a broader paraphrase.

7.s:
With reference to the Law Commission of India, consider the following statements:
1. It is an executive body established by a Government of India order for a fixed three-year term.
2. It is an advisory body and not a quasi-judicial body.
3. It submits its reports to the President of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Commission reports to the Ministry of Law and Justice, not to the President, making statement 3 false.
7.tq: Check the body’s legal status and reporting authority separately.

7.s: Who chaired the first Law Commission established after India’s Independence?
7.x: The first post-Independence Law Commission was established in 1955 and was chaired by M.C. Setalvad.
7.tq: Use the historical chairperson rather than confusing the colonial precursor with the post-Independence body.

7.s: The colonial Law Commission associated with the production of the Indian Penal Code was chaired by:
7.x: Macaulay’s Law Commission was the colonial precursor and produced the Indian Penal Code in 1860.
7.tq: Separate the colonial precursor from the first post-Independence Law Commission.

7.s: The Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 was formed primarily to examine:
7.x: The JPC chaired by P.P. Chaudhary examined the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, concerning simultaneous elections. The Bill was introduced on 17 December 2024.
7.tq: Link the committee’s subject with the Bill under examination.

7.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: JPC on Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill — D. Purandeswari
JPC on VBSA Bill, 2025 — P.P. Chaudhary
JPC on VBSA Bill, 2025 — D. Purandeswari
7.x: D. Purandeswari chaired the 31-member JPC on the VBSA Bill, 2025, which concerned a single higher-education regulator.
7.tq: Use chairperson–committee matching and reject swapped names.

7.s: The Public Accounts Committee for 2026–27 is chaired by:
7.x: K.C. Venugopal is the chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee for 2026–27, which examines CAG audit reports.
7.tq: Identify the chairperson through the committee’s current year and subject.

7.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Public Accounts Committee:
1. It was set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919.
2. It consists of 22 members, including 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
3. A Minister can be a member of the Committee.
4. It has been chaired by a member of the Opposition since 1967.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. A Minister cannot be a member of the Public Accounts Committee, so statement 3 is false.
7.tq: Find the exception in the committee’s composition and chairpersonship rules.

7.s: The National Crime Records Bureau was established in 1986 by:
o: A resolution of the United Nations
An Act of Parliament following the Sarkaria Commission
An executive order following the Tandon Committee
7.x: The NCRB was set up in 1986 by executive order after the Tandon Committee. It functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
7.tq: Distinguish an executive creation from a statutory or constitutional body.

7.s: Which organisation publishes the report ‘Crime in India’?
7.x: Crime in India is published by the National Crime Records Bureau under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
7.tq: Match the national report with its publishing body.

7.s: According to Crime in India 2024, which State recorded the highest number of human-trafficking cases?
7.x: Telangana recorded the highest number of human-trafficking cases in the stated Crime in India 2024 data.
7.tq: Separate the ranking category from other crime indicators.

7.s: Which State had the highest violent-crime rate in the Crime in India 2024 data?
7.x: Odisha had the highest violent-crime rate in the stated Crime in India 2024 data.
7.tq: Do not interchange the State rankings for trafficking and violent crime.

7.s: Among metropolitan cities, which city recorded the highest number of cybercrime cases in the Crime in India 2024 data?
7.x: Bengaluru recorded the highest number of cybercrime cases among metropolitan cities in the stated data.
7.tq: Match the crime category with the correct metropolitan ranking.

7.s: Who was appointed as the chief of the National Crime Records Bureau in July 2026?
7.x: Amit Garg was appointed as the chief of the National Crime Records Bureau in July 2026.
7.tq: Match the current appointment with the correct institution.

7.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey is conducted by the:
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
7.x: PLFS is conducted by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation; it has been released monthly since 2025.
7.tq: Match the survey with its conducting agency and ministry.

7.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NFHS — MoHFW, with IIPS Mumbai as nodal institution
7.x: NFHS is conducted under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, with the International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai, as the nodal institution.
7.tq: Begin with the known survey–agency pair and eliminate cross-swapped agencies.

7.s: The Annual Status of Education Report is conducted by:
7.x: ASER is conducted by Pratham, a non-governmental organisation.
7.tq: Distinguish the NGO-led survey from government surveys.

7.s: The Household Consumption Expenditure Survey for 2022–23 and 2023–24 is published by the:
7.x: HCES 2022–23 and 2023–24 are conducted by the NSO under MoSPI and provide weights for the new CPI introduced in 2024.
7.tq: Link the survey to both its agency and its stated statistical use.

7.s: Which of the following statements regarding AISHE is correct?
o: It is conducted by Pratham and measures household consumption.
It is conducted by the Ministry of Education, and the 2022–23 and 2023–24 editions were released together in July 2026.
It is conducted by the Registrar General of India as part of the Census.
It is conducted by NITI Aayog to prepare the SDG Index.
7.x: AISHE is conducted by the Ministry of Education. The 2022–23 and 2023–24 reports were released together in July 2026, when undergraduate enrolment fell for the first time.
7.tq: Use the conducting ministry and release detail to reject familiar agency swaps.

7.s: The Sample Registration System 2024 is associated with which agency?
7.x: SRS 2024 is associated with the Registrar General of India.
7.tq: Match the demographic survey with the registration authority.

7.s: Census 2027 is being conducted by the:
o: Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs
NITI Aayog under the Cabinet Secretariat
7.x: Census 2027 is being conducted by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs. It is the first digital Census, with houselisting in 2026.
7.tq: Identify the statutory census authority rather than a general statistical agency.

7.s: Which organisation publishes the Export Preparedness Index?
o: Ministry of Commerce and Industry alone
7.x: The Export Preparedness Index 2024, its fourth edition, is published by NITI Aayog.
7.tq: Match the index with its central publishing agency.

7.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to the Export Preparedness Index 2024:
1. Maharashtra — first among large States
2. Tamil Nadu — second among large States
3. Gujarat — third among large States
4. Andhra Pradesh — fifth among large States
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
7.x: The stated order among large States is Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh. Therefore all four pairs are correct.
7.tq: Read the ranking sequence carefully and test each position.

7.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Fiscal Health Index 2026?
o: Arunachal Pradesh — last among North-Eastern and Himalayan States
Andhra Pradesh — first among major States
7.x: Odisha ranked first among major States in the Fiscal Health Index 2026, while Punjab ranked last. Arunachal Pradesh ranked first among North-Eastern and Himalayan States, and Andhra Pradesh ranked 17th.
7.tq: Separate categories of States before comparing their rankings.

7.s: Which of the following indices is published by NITI Aayog?
7.x: The SDG India Index, Composite Water Management Index, School Education Quality Index and Health Index are associated with NITI Aayog. The Good Governance Index is associated with DARPG.
7.tq: Use the agency–index association and avoid ministry swaps.

7.s: The Good Governance Index is published by the:
o: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
7.x: The Good Governance Index is published by DARPG and includes sectors such as grievance redressal and e-governance.
7.tq: Match the governance index with the department responsible for administrative reforms.

7.s: Who is the latest chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission?
7.x: Justice V. Ramasubramanian is the latest chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission.
7.tq: Match the newly appointed chairperson with the correct commission.

7.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
7.x: Arvind Panagariya is the chairperson of the 16th Finance Commission, not the National Commission for Minorities. NCM is chaired by Harjit Singh Grewal.
7.tq: Find the swapped chairperson–commission pair.

7.s: Who is the Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog according to the stated appointments?
7.x: Ashok Kumar Lahiri is the Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog. Arvind Panagariya chairs the 16th Finance Commission.
7.tq: Distinguish the executive policy body’s vice-chairperson from a commission chairperson.

7.s: The Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities, appointed for a three-year term, is:
7.x: Harjit Singh Grewal is the Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities for a three-year term.
7.tq: Use the tenure detail to identify the correct appointment.

7.s:
With reference to the 2019 amendment concerning the National Human Rights Commission, consider the following statements:
1. An SC judge, and not only a former Chief Justice of India, can be appointed as its chairperson.
2. The chairperson’s term is three years or until attaining the age of 70 years.
3. The chairpersons of the NCBC and NCPCR are deemed members of the NHRC.
4. The Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities is deemed a member of the NHRC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: All four statements are correct. The 2019 amendment broadened eligibility for the NHRC chairperson and included the specified commission chairpersons and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities as deemed members.
7.tq: Check each statutory amendment detail instead of assuming the earlier composition continues.

7.s: The award of which Finance Commission came into force on 1 April 2026?
7.x: The award of the 16th Finance Commission came into force on 1 April 2026.
7.tq: Use the exact year and date to distinguish closely numbered commissions.

7.s: Which of the following was introduced as a new criterion in the award of the 16th Finance Commission?
7.x: Contribution to GDP was introduced as a new criterion in the 16th Finance Commission award.
7.tq: Identify the newly added criterion rather than a familiar older parameter.

7.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the criticism of the 16th Finance Commission award:
1. Revenue-deficit grants were dropped.
2. The weight assigned to income distance was reduced.
3. The changes were viewed as placing efficiency above equity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: All three statements are correct: revenue-deficit grants were dropped, the income-distance weight was reduced, and the resulting approach was criticised for prioritising efficiency over equity.
7.tq: Check whether all linked features of a policy criticism are simultaneously present.

7.s: Under the 16th Finance Commission, the devolution share associated with Andhra Pradesh was reported as:
7.x: Andhra Pradesh's devolution share under the 16th Finance Commission was reported as 4.2%.
7.tq: Distinguish the exact percentage from nearby numerical distractors.

7.s: Which demand was pressed by Andhra Pradesh in relation to the criteria of the 16th Finance Commission?
7.x: Andhra Pradesh pressed for greater weight to capital needs in the Finance Commission criteria.
7.tq: Match the concerned State with its specific policy demand.

7.s: In July 2026, which of the following was associated with the exam-reform task force?
o: The Chairperson of the State Commission for Scheduled Tribes
The Chairman of the Finance Commission
7.x: Nilekani was associated with the exam-reform task force announced in July 2026.
7.tq: Link the person to the correct task force instead of the similarly current commissions.

7.s: The VBSA Bill was associated with which of the following parliamentary mechanisms?
7.x: The VBSA Bill was associated with the Joint Parliamentary Committee.
7.tq: Apply the ‘which body?’ test to distinguish parliamentary committees.

7.s: Which State was reported to have secured a change in the VBSA framework relating to State consent?
7.x: Andhra Pradesh was reported to have secured the change relating to State consent in the VBSA framework.
7.tq: Match the State with the specific institutional change it secured.

7.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh's positions in the two indices mentioned for 2024:
1. Andhra Pradesh ranked fifth in the EPI 2024.
2. Andhra Pradesh ranked seventeenth in the FHI.
3. Andhra Pradesh ranked seventeenth in the EPI 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
7.x: Andhra Pradesh ranked fifth in EPI 2024 and seventeenth in FHI. The statement placing it seventeenth in EPI 2024 is incorrect.
7.tq: Separate the two index names before comparing their ranks.

7.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: IMF — India’s national accounts received an A grade
7.x: Delayed NCRB/AISHE data was identified as an issue. India’s national accounts received a C grade from the IMF, while Andhra Pradesh ranked fifth in EPI 2024 and seventeenth in FHI.
7.tq: Find the one correctly matched pair after checking the swapped rankings and grade.

7.s: What grade did the International Monetary Fund assign to India's national accounts?
7.x: The IMF assigned a C grade to India's national accounts.
7.tq: Recall the exact grade and reject adjacent alphabetical alternatives.

8.s: The 17th BRICS Summit held in July 2025 was hosted at which of the following places?
8.x: The 17th BRICS Summit was held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in July 2025.
8.tq: Direct venue recall using nearby summit locations as distractors.

8.s: Who chaired the 17th BRICS Summit held in 2025?
8.x: Lula da Silva, the President of Brazil, chaired the 17th BRICS Summit held in Rio de Janeiro in July 2025.
8.tq: Who-chaired-which-summit discrimination.

8.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 18th BRICS Summit:
1. It was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
2. It was held on 12–13 September 2026.
3. India handed over the BRICS chair to China for 2027.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: All three statements are correct. The 18th BRICS Summit was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 12–13 September 2026, and the chair was to pass from India to China for 2027.
8.tq: Statement combination testing venue, date and chair handover.

8.s: The theme of the 18th BRICS Summit held in New Delhi was:
o: One Earth, One Family, One Future
Upholding the Shanghai Spirit: SCO on the Move
Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability
8.x: The theme of the 18th BRICS Summit was “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”
8.tq: Exact-theme recall with themes of other groupings as traps.

8.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
8.x: The 20th G20 Summit was held in Johannesburg, South Africa, in November 2025. It was the first G20 Summit held on African soil.
8.tq: Start from the sure venue-edition pair and eliminate swapped summit locations.

8.s: The theme of the 20th G20 Summit hosted by South Africa in 2025 was associated with which of the following?
o: Working Together to Address Major International Challenges
Solidarity, Equality, and Sustainability; the spirit of Ubuntu
Inclusivity and Sustainability; ASEAN rotational chairmanship
8.x: The 20th G20 Summit adopted the theme “Solidarity, Equality, and Sustainability”, reflecting the philosophy of Ubuntu, or “I am because we are.”
8.tq: Theme-and-host association using exact official wording.

8.s:
Arrange the following summits in chronological order according to their editions:
A. 18th BRICS Summit
B. 20th G20 Summit
C. 25th SCO Summit
D. 52nd G7 Summit
8.x: The 20th G20 Summit was held in November 2025, followed by the 25th SCO Summit in August–September 2025 in the edition sequence presented here; the 18th BRICS Summit and 52nd G7 Summit were held in 2026. Thus, among the listed summit events by date, the proper order is G20, SCO, BRICS, G7.
8.tq: Use the dates first and then check the middle positions carefully.

8.s: The 25th Summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation was held at:
8.x: The 25th SCO Summit was held in Tianjin, China, on 31 August–1 September 2025. China hosted the SCO Summit for the fifth time.
8.tq: Edition-to-venue matching with confusable SCO and ASEAN venues.

8.s: Which of the following is the theme of the 25th SCO Summit held in China?
o: Upholding the Shanghai Spirit: SCO on the Move
Together for Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity
Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability
8.x: The theme of the 25th SCO Summit was “Upholding the Shanghai Spirit: SCO on the Move.”
8.tq: Exact-theme discrimination among summit slogans.

8.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 26th SCO Summit:
1. It is scheduled to be held in Bishkek.
2. Kyrgyzstan is the host country.
3. Its theme refers to 25 years of the SCO.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: All three statements are correct. The 26th SCO Summit is scheduled at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan in 2026, with the theme “25 Years of SCO: Together for Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity.”
8.tq: Combine venue, host and theme clues without confusing the 25th and 26th editions.

8.s: The 52nd G7 Summit, scheduled for June 2026, was hosted at Évian-les-Bains under the chairmanship of:
8.x: The 52nd G7 Summit was held at Évian-les-Bains, France, in June 2026, under the chairmanship of Emmanuel Macron.
8.tq: Chairperson-and-host matching; reject leaders associated with other summits or years.

8.s: Which of the following statements about the 52nd G7 Summit is correct?
o: Its chair was Lula da Silva of Brazil.
The United States hosted the 52nd G7 Summit in 2026.
Its theme was “Working Together to Address Major International Challenges”.
It was held in Kananaskis, Canada, in June 2026.
8.x: The 52nd G7 Summit was held in Évian-les-Bains, France, under Emmanuel Macron, with the theme “Working Together to Address Major International Challenges.”
8.tq: Find the one precisely matched statement among year, venue and chair swaps.

8.s: The 22nd ASEAN–India Summit was held in which manner and under whose chair?
o: Physically in Bangkok under Thailand’s chair
Virtually under China’s chair as part of the SCO Summit
Physically in New Delhi under India’s chair
Virtually under Malaysia’s chair as part of the 47th ASEAN Summit
8.x: The 22nd ASEAN–India Summit was held virtually under Malaysia’s chair and formed part of the 47th ASEAN Summit in Kuala Lumpur in October 2025.
8.tq: Split the option into format, chair and institutional setting before choosing.

8.s: Which of the following was NOT an outcome associated with the 22nd ASEAN–India Summit?
o: Call for an early review of AITIGA
Adoption of the Shanghai Spirit as the guiding principle
ASEAN–India Comprehensive Strategic Partnership plan for 2026–2030
Declaration of 2026 as the ASEAN–India Year of Maritime Cooperation
8.x: The Shanghai Spirit was associated with the 25th SCO Summit. The ASEAN–India Summit outcomes included the maritime cooperation year, the 2026–2030 partnership plan and an early AITIGA review.
8.tq: Find the outcome belonging to another regional grouping.

8.s:
Consider the following statements about the Quad during 2025–2026:
1. No Quad leaders’ summit was held in 2025.
2. India hosted the 11th Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in New Delhi in May 2026.
3. The Quad had six leader-level summits during 2021–2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: All three statements are correct. No Quad leaders’ summit was held in 2025; India hosted the 11th Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in New Delhi on 26 May 2026, and six leader-level summits occurred during 2021–2024.
8.tq: Test several closely related numerical and event-status statements together.

8.s: Which one of the following statements regarding SAARC is correct?
o: Its last summit was held at Thimphu in 2025 and it is fully active.

8.x: The summit resulted in a Joint Declaration on Economic Security covering five sectors.
8.tq: Retain both the policy area and the exact number of sectors.

8.s:
With reference to India's G20 Presidency, consider the following statements:
1. India hosted the 18th G20 Summit.
2. The Summit was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
3. The theme of the Summit was “One Earth, One Family, One Future”.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: India hosted the 18th G20 Summit at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 9–10 September 2023. Its theme was “One Earth, One Family, One Future”.
8.tq: Combine three directly related factual statements and identify the option containing all correct details.

8.s: The 18th G20 Summit hosted by India was held on:
8.x: The 18th G20 Summit was held in New Delhi on 9–10 September 2023.
8.tq: Direct date recall using closely spaced date distractors.

8.s: Which of the following was the headline outcome of the 18th G20 Summit hosted by India?
o: Admission of Timor-Leste as an ASEAN member
Adoption of the Glasgow Climate Pact
Admission of the African Union as a permanent member
Creation of the Loss and Damage Fund
8.x: The African Union was admitted as a permanent member of the G20 during India's Presidency.
8.tq: Distinguish the principal summit outcome from outcomes associated with other international groupings or summits.

8.s: Which one of the following was NOT launched under India's G20 Presidency?
8.x: The Global Biofuels Alliance, MAHARISHI and the Global Initiative on Digital Health were launched under India's G20 Presidency. The Loss and Damage Fund is associated with COP27.
8.tq: Find the item belonging to a nearby but different international summit.

8.s: The MAHARISHI initiative launched under India's G20 Presidency is associated with:
8.x: MAHARISHI was launched as an initiative relating to research on millets.
8.tq: Match an initiative with its precise subject rather than with another G20 initiative.

8.s: Which of the following initiatives was launched under India's G20 Presidency specifically for climate monitoring?
8.x: A “G20 satellite” was launched under India's G20 Presidency for climate monitoring.
8.tq: Direct initiative-purpose discrimination.

8.s: India's G20 Presidency lasted from:
8.x: India held the G20 Presidency from 1 December 2022 to 30 November 2023.
8.tq: Test an exact tenure using four closely related date ranges.

8.s: During India's G20 Presidency, meetings were spread across approximately how many cities covering all States and Union Territories?
8.x: G20 meetings during India's Presidency were held across about 60 cities in all States and Union Territories.
8.tq: Numerical recall with rounded scale-based distractors.

8.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Initiative)
a. International Solar Alliance
b. CDRI
c. Global Biofuels Alliance
 d. ACITI

List-II (Launch context)
i. India's G20 Presidency, 2023
ii. COP21, Paris, 2015
iii. UN Climate Action Summit, 2019
iv. G20 Johannesburg sidelines, November 2025

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
8.x: The International Solar Alliance was launched at COP21; CDRI at the 2019 UN Climate Action Summit; the Global Biofuels Alliance during India's 2023 G20 Presidency; and ACITI on the sidelines of G20 Johannesburg in November 2025.
8.tq: Start from the sure launch-context pair and eliminate codes.

8.s: The International Solar Alliance was launched jointly by:
8.x: The International Solar Alliance was launched by India and France at COP21 in Paris in 2015.
8.tq: Direct founder-pair recall with distractors drawn from other initiatives.

8.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the International Solar Alliance is correct?
o: It is headquartered in Stockholm and was founded by India and Sweden.
Its secretariat is at New Delhi and it was launched at COP29 in Baku.
Its headquarters is at Gurugram and it is the first intergovernmental body headquartered in India.
It is headquartered in Paris and deals exclusively with nuclear energy.
8.x: The International Solar Alliance has its headquarters at Gurugram and is the first intergovernmental body headquartered in India.
8.tq: Use the headquarters and institutional-status distinction to reject swapped-location options.

8.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. CDRI was launched at the UN Climate Action Summit in 2019.
2. The secretariat of CDRI is located in New Delhi.
3. CDRI is associated with sustainable biofuels.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: CDRI was launched at the 2019 UN Climate Action Summit and has its secretariat in New Delhi. Sustainable biofuels are associated with the Global Biofuels Alliance, not CDRI.
8.tq: Identify one swapped subject-area statement among two correct institutional facts.

8.s: The Digital Innovation Alliance launched at G20 2025 was promoted by:
8.x: The Digital Innovation Alliance at G20 2025 was launched by India, Brazil and South Africa as a DPI-based Global South alternative.
8.tq: Founder-group identification with country combinations from related initiatives.

8.s:
The Tropical Forest Forever Facility, associated with COP30, has which of the following features?
1. It is Brazil-led.
2. It involves US$125 billion.
3. India joined it as an Observer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: The Tropical Forest Forever Facility is Brazil-led, involves US$125 billion, and India joined it as an Observer.
8.tq: Check a three-part institutional description without confusing it with the COP outcome itself.

8.s: LeadIT, co-chaired by India and Sweden at COP29 in Baku, is concerned primarily with:
o: Expansion of solar power in tropical countries
Digital public infrastructure for the Global South
Sharing benefits from digital sequence information
Transition of heavy industry, including steel and cement
8.x: LeadIT focuses on the transition of heavy industries such as steel and cement.
8.tq: Link the initiative to the sector named in its policy objective.

8.s: Which of the following proposals was included among India's proposals at G20 2025?
8.x: The Africa Skills Multiplier was one of India's G20 2025 proposals, aiming at one million trainers over a decade.
8.tq: Separate a national proposal from formal outcomes of climate and biodiversity conferences.

8.s: The Africa Skills Multiplier proposed by India envisages:
o: One million solar panels in five years
One million digital health workers in one year
One million trainers in a decade
One million hectares of forest by 2030
8.x: The Africa Skills Multiplier proposal envisages one million trainers over a decade.
8.tq: Test the distinctive numerical target attached to a named proposal.

8.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among India's G20 2025 proposals?
8.x: India's proposals included Countering the Drug-Terror Nexus, the Global Traditional Knowledge Repository and the Critical Minerals Circularity Initiative. The Baku-to-Belém Roadmap is associated with COP29.
8.tq: Find the outcome belonging to another summit and subject cluster.

8.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the expansion of BRICS?
1. BRIC was coined in 2001 by Jim O'Neill.
2. South Africa joined in 2011.
3. Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE joined in 2024.
4. Indonesia joined in January 2025.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
8.x: Jim O'Neill coined BRIC in 2001; South Africa joined in 2011; Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE joined in 2024; and Indonesia joined in January 2025.
8.tq: Build the chronology of membership changes from the earliest coinage to the latest admission.

8.s: Which country was invited to BRICS but had not formally confirmed its membership?
8.x: Saudi Arabia was invited to BRICS but had not formally confirmed its membership, although some listings count it as a member.
8.tq: Test the distinction between invitation, formal confirmation and listing practice.

8.s: Apart from its full-member count, the expanded BRICS grouping includes approximately how many partner countries?
8.x: The expanded BRICS grouping is described as having approximately 10 partner countries, including Belarus, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand and Vietnam.
8.tq: Recall the numerical distinction between full members and partner countries.

8.s: Which of the following countries is listed as an example of a BRICS partner country?
8.x: Belarus is among the examples of BRICS partner countries; Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand and Vietnam are other examples.
8.tq: Identify a member of a named partner grouping rather than a full member or unrelated major economy.

8.s: The African Union was admitted as a permanent member of the G20 in 2023 and was fully operationalised at:
8.x: The African Union's permanent membership in the G20 was fully operationalised at Johannesburg in 2025.
8.tq: Distinguish the year of admission from the later operationalisation of membership.

8.s: Timor-Leste became the 11th member of ASEAN and attended its first summit as a full member in:
8.x: Timor-Leste became ASEAN's 11th member and attended its first summit as a full member in October 2025.
8.tq: Direct membership-and-date recall using adjacent years as distractors.

8.s: The East Asia Summit currently has:
8.x: The East Asia Summit has 19 members, comprising 11 ASEAN members and 8 partners.
8.tq: Split the total into its two components before selecting the matching composition.

8.s: Russia's position in the G7/G8 framework is correctly described by which statement?
o: It was admitted in 1998 and suspended in 2014 after Crimea.
It was admitted in 2014 and suspended in 1998 after Crimea.
It was never admitted to the G8.
It became a permanent G7 member in 2024.
8.x: Russia was admitted in 1998, creating the G8, and was suspended in 2014 after the Crimea episode.
8.tq: Arrange the two membership events in their correct historical sequence.

8.s:
Match the following Climate COPs with their venues and principal outcomes:
A. COP21
B. COP26
C. COP27
D. COP28

1. Glasgow Climate Pact and India's Panchamrit
2. Paris Agreement
3. Loss and Damage Fund
4. Global Stocktake and “transition away” from fossil fuels

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
8.x: COP21 in Paris produced the Paris Agreement; COP26 in Glasgow produced the Glasgow Climate Pact; COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh produced the Loss and Damage Fund; and COP28 in Dubai produced the Global Stocktake and the “transition away” wording.
8.tq: Start with the well-known Paris Agreement pair and complete the summit-outcome matches.

8.s: The Paris Agreement was adopted on 12 December 2015 and entered into force on:
8.x: The Paris Agreement was adopted on 12 December 2015 and entered into force on 4 November 2016.
8.tq: Distinguish adoption and entry-into-force dates rather than treating them as one event.

8.s: India's Panchamrit was associated with:
8.x: India's Panchamrit was associated with COP26, held at Glasgow in 2021.
8.tq: Match a national climate initiative with the correct COP venue and year.

8.s: The Loss and Damage Fund was associated with:
8.x: The Loss and Damage Fund was an outcome associated with COP27 at Sharm el-Sheikh in 2022.
8.tq: Discriminate among successive COP outcomes.

8.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal outcome of COP28?
o: Adoption of the Glasgow Climate Pact
Adoption of the Paris Agreement and entry into force provisions
Global Stocktake and the call for a “transition away” from fossil fuels
Creation of the Loss and Damage Fund
8.x: COP28 in Dubai produced the Global Stocktake and included the wording on transitioning away from fossil fuels.
8.tq: Use the exact outcome phrase to distinguish COP28 from COP26 and COP27.

8.s:
Consider the following statements regarding COP29:
1. It was held at Baku.
2. It set a new collective quantified finance goal of US$300 billion annually by 2035.
3. It proposed the Baku-to-Belém Roadmap to US$1.3 trillion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: COP29 was held at Baku in 2024. Its outcomes included the US$300 billion annual finance goal by 2035 and the Baku-to-Belém Roadmap targeting US$1.3 trillion.
8.tq: Combine venue, acronym-related finance outcome and numerical target in one coded question.

8.s: COP30 was held at Belém, Brazil, and was notable because it was:
o: The first COP held under the UNFCCC
The first COP held in a G7 country
The first COP held in Europe
The first COP held in the Amazon
8.x: COP30, held in Belém in November 2025, was the first COP held in the Amazon region.
8.tq: Identify the distinctive geographical feature of the venue.

8.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with the Belém Political Package of COP30?
o: A roadmap for the complete phase-out of fossil fuels
Belém Action Mechanism on just transition
60 indicators for the Global Goal on Adaptation
8.x: The COP30 outcomes included tripling adaptation finance by 2035, the Belém Action Mechanism and 60 Global Goal on Adaptation indicators. No fossil-fuel roadmap was adopted.
8.tq: Locate the precise exception among several outcomes from the same summit.

8.s: The phrase “global mutirão” is associated with the:
8.x: “Global mutirão” formed part of the Belém Political Package adopted at COP30.
8.tq: Test recognition of a distinctive official phrase and its summit context.

8.s: Which of the following is the correct pairing regarding future Climate COPs?
8.x: COP31 is scheduled for Antalya, Türkiye, in November 2026, while COP32 is scheduled for Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in 2027.
8.tq: Match consecutive future editions with their venues without reversing the sequence.

8.s:
With reference to COP31, consider the following statements:
1. Türkiye holds the presidency.
2. Australia presides over the negotiations.
3. It is scheduled for November 2026 at Antalya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: COP31 is scheduled for November 2026 at Antalya, Türkiye; Türkiye holds the presidency and Australia presides over the negotiations.
8.tq: Separate host-country presidency from the country presiding over negotiations.

8.s: Which statement regarding India's proposed hosting of COP33 is correct?
o: India won the bid and will host COP33 in 2028.
India has hosted COP33 and is bidding for COP34.
India withdrew its bid, leaving South Korea as the only other contender.
India withdrew its bid after COP21, leaving Brazil as the only contender.
8.x: India withdrew its COP33 bid through an Environment Ministry letter dated 2 April 2026, reported on 9 April 2026; South Korea was the only other contender.
8.tq: Use the status of a bid rather than assuming that a bid means successful hosting.

8.s: How many times has India hosted a UN Climate Change COP, according to the given record?
o: Three times, COP8, COP26 and COP33
8.x: India has hosted only COP8, held in 2002.
8.tq: Distinguish hosting from participation, bidding or association with another COP outcome.

8.s: Which of the following correctly matches the biodiversity COP outcome?
o: CBD COP16—Cali Fund on digital sequence information benefit-sharing
8.x: CBD COP16 at Cali, resumed at Rome, was associated with the Cali Fund on digital sequence information benefit-sharing. COP15 produced the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.
8.tq: Separate biodiversity-convention outcomes from UNFCCC climate outcomes.

8.s: The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework is associated with the target popularly known as:
8.x: The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework is associated with the 30x30 target.
8.tq: Recall the numerical shorthand attached to a named international framework.

8.s: The first Convention on Biological Diversity COP was held at:
8.x: The first CBD COP was held at Nassau, Bahamas, in 1994.
8.tq: Direct venue-and-year recall with later biodiversity COP venues as distractors.

8.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC):
1. It was adopted on 9 May 1992 at the Rio Earth Summit.
2. It entered into force on 21 March 1994.
3. It has 198 Parties.
4. Its secretariat is located at Bonn.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: The UNFCCC was adopted on 9 May 1992 at the Rio Earth Summit, entered into force on 21 March 1994, has 198 Parties and has its secretariat at Bonn.
8.tq: Test a complete treaty profile through date, membership and headquarters statements.

8.s: At the Bonn Subsidiary Bodies session in June 2026, India pressed for dialogue on unilateral trade measures such as:
8.x: India pressed at the June 2026 Bonn Subsidiary Bodies session for dialogue on unilateral trade measures such as the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM).
8.tq: Identify the policy instrument from a current climate-negotiation context.

8.s: The 18th BRICS Summit hosted by India was held at which place during 12–13 September 2026?
8.x: India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on 12–13 September 2026.
8.tq: Use the place and date together to distinguish the summit from other BRICS-related events.

8.s: To which country did India hand over the BRICS chairship after the 18th BRICS Summit in September 2026?
8.x: India handed over the BRICS chairship to China on 14 September 2026.
8.tq: Track the outgoing and incoming chair rather than confusing summit host with the next chair.

8.s: The G20 Summit of 2025 was significant because it was the first G20 Summit held on which continent?
8.x: The G20 Summit of 2025 was the first G20 Summit held on African soil.
8.tq: Identify the significance attached to the first occurrence.

8.s: The AI Impact Summit 2026 was described as the first global AI summit to be held in which region?
8.x: The AI Impact Summit 2026 was described as the first global AI summit held in the Global South.
8.tq: Distinguish the geographical description of the venue from the name of the summit.

8.s: The first COP held in the Amazon was associated with which year?
8.x: The first COP in the Amazon was held in 2025.
8.tq: Use the year-based first-occurrence clue to eliminate nearby dates.

8.s: The CII Partnership Summit 2025, held on 14–15 November 2025, was hosted at which place?
8.x: The CII Partnership Summit 2025 was held in Visakhapatnam on 14–15 November 2025.
8.tq: Combine the event date with its location to avoid confusing it with other Andhra Pradesh venues.

8.s: What was the theme of the CII Partnership Summit 2025 held in Visakhapatnam?
o: One Earth, One Economy, One Future
Transforming Andhra Pradesh into a Trillion-Dollar Economy
Building a Digital India for the Global South
Andhra Pradesh as the Gateway to Southeast Asia
8.x: The theme was “Transforming Andhra Pradesh into a Trillion-Dollar Economy.”
8.tq: Discriminate the exact official theme from broad economic-development phrases.

8.s: What amount of investment was committed at the CII Partnership Summit 2025 in Visakhapatnam?
8.x: Investment commitments at the summit amounted to ₹2,80,384 crore.
8.tq: Test the precise figure by separating similar-looking numerical alternatives.

8.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the CII Partnership Summit 2025:
1. It involved 193 proposals.
2. It was associated with the creation of 5,01,746 jobs.
3. It was held in New Delhi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: The summit involved 193 proposals and 5,01,746 jobs. Statement 3 is false because the summit was held in Visakhapatnam.
8.tq: Find the wrong location statement while retaining the correct numerical details.

8.s: BRICS National Security Advisers were unable to agree on a joint statement in June 2026 primarily on which issue?
8.x: BRICS National Security Advisers could not agree on a joint statement concerning terrorism in June 2026.
8.tq: Match the diplomatic deadlock with the specific issue that caused it.

8.s: Which statement reflects China’s position expressed in the debate concerning the Global South?
o: The Global South is confined exclusively to Africa.
China should withdraw from all Global South institutions.
A Global South without China is not real.
The Global South should exclude all major economies.
8.x: China stated that a “Global South without China” is not real.
8.tq: Recognise the exact political formulation rather than a broad paraphrase.

8.s: Which country assumed the chairship of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation in 2026?
8.x: Pakistan assumed the chairship of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation in 2026.
8.tq: Apply the ‘who chairs the organisation’ approach instead of confusing SCO chairship with BRICS chairship.

8.s: Which of the following followed the commitment made at Davos 2026 in the context of Andhra Pradesh’s international economic engagement?
o: AP–UAE Food Cluster Memorandum of Understanding
8.x: The AP–UAE Food Cluster MoU in July 2026 followed the commitment made at Davos 2026.
8.tq: Link the later agreement with the earlier summit commitment and identify the correct partner.

8.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recent international summit developments:
1. The United States skipped the G20 Summit of 2025.
2. The United States skipped COP30.
3. The Quad Leaders’ Summit stalled.
4. COP30 pledges were voluntary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
8.x: All four statements are correct: the United States skipped the G20 2025 and COP30, the Quad Leaders’ Summit stalled, and COP30 pledges were voluntary.
8.tq: Verify each statement independently before selecting the complete combination.

9.s: Which of the following countries joined BRICS from 1 January 2024?
o: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates
Argentina, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia and Egypt
Ethiopia, Saudi Arabia, Indonesia and the United Arab Emirates
9.x: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates joined BRICS from 1 January 2024. Argentina declined the invitation, while Indonesia joined in 2025 and Saudi Arabia's status remained unconfirmed.
9.tq: Use the exact admission date and separate invited, admitted and unconfirmed members.

9.s:
Consider the following statements regarding recent changes in international groupings:
1. Indonesia joined BRICS in January 2025.
2. Timor-Leste became the eleventh member of ASEAN in October 2025.
3. Finland and Sweden became the 31st and 32nd members of NATO, respectively.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. Indonesia joined BRICS in January 2025, Timor-Leste became ASEAN's eleventh member in October 2025, and Finland and Sweden became NATO's 31st and 32nd members.
9.tq: Combine closely related membership changes and verify the sequence and ordinal numbers.

9.s: The tenth member and the first Central Asian member of the New Development Bank is:
9.x: Uzbekistan became the tenth member of the New Development Bank and its first member from Central Asia. The headquarters of the Bank is in Shanghai.
9.tq: Discriminate between neighbouring countries using the ordinal and regional description.

9.s: The headquarters of the New Development Bank is located at:
9.x: The New Development Bank is headquartered in Shanghai, China.
9.tq: Test the headquarters separately from the organisation's membership changes.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: New Development Bank — Chair in 2026: Uzbekistan
9.x: Bangladesh is the BIMSTEC chair for 2026. The other pairings incorrectly assign leadership roles not stated for those organisations.
9.tq: Find the organisation–current chair pair rather than confusing membership with chairmanship.

9.s: Bulgaria and Romania became full members of the Schengen Area from:
9.x: Bulgaria and Romania became full members of the Schengen Area on 1 January 2025.
9.tq: Use the precise date to distinguish partial or earlier accession from full membership.

9.s:
With reference to the Colombo Security Conclave, consider the following statements:
1. It was formed in 2020.
2. Bangladesh is its sixth member.
3. Seychelles is included among its members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: The Colombo Security Conclave was formed in 2020 and comprises India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh and Seychelles. Thus all three statements are correct.
9.tq: Check the membership list and the numerical description of the grouping.

9.s: Which of the following correctly describes the composition of the G20 as given in the current grouping?
o: 19 countries, the European Union and the African Union
19 countries and only the African Union
18 countries, the European Union and ASEAN
9.x: The grouping consists of 19 countries, the European Union and the African Union. The African Union became a member in 2023.
9.tq: Avoid the numerical trap by separating countries from regional organisations.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kimberley Process:
1. It consists of 59 countries and the European Union.
2. India is a founding member.
3. India assumed its chairmanship from 1 January 2026 for the third time.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: The Kimberley Process comprises 60 participants—59 countries and the European Union. India is a founding member and took over its chairmanship on 1 January 2026 for the third time.
9.tq: Convert a composition figure and leadership details into a coded statement question.

9.s: Which of the following statements regarding India's international memberships is correct?
o: India is a full member of APEC, whose Secretariat is in Singapore.
India joined APEC along with Timor-Leste in 2025.
India is a founding member of APEC with veto power.
India is not a member of APEC and has only observer status.
9.x: India is not a member of APEC and is only an observer. APEC has 21 economies and its Secretariat is located in Singapore.
9.tq: Discriminate between participation, observer status and full membership.

9.s: The 2025 APEC summit was held at:
9.x: The 2025 APEC summit was held in Gyeongju, South Korea. Singapore is the location of the APEC Secretariat, not the summit venue.
9.tq: Separate the summit venue from the organisation's permanent secretariat location.

9.s: Pax Silica, which India joined in February 2026, is associated primarily with:
o: Critical minerals, semiconductors and artificial-intelligence supply chains
International civil aviation and airport security
Nuclear disarmament and strategic arms reduction
9.x: Pax Silica is a US-led initiative concerning critical minerals, semiconductor supply chains and artificial intelligence supply chains.
9.tq: Identify the sector governed by the initiative instead of its geographical or political label.

9.s: The United States announced its intention to quit how many international bodies, comprising non-UN and UN bodies respectively?
9.x: The United States announced its intention to quit 66 bodies—35 non-UN bodies and 31 UN bodies. The listed bodies included WHO, UNFCCC, IPCC, ISA, IRENA, UNHRC and UNESCO.
9.tq: Retain the total and its two-part numerical breakdown together.

9.s: The United States left the Paris Agreement for the second time in:
9.x: The United States left the Paris Agreement for the second time in January 2026.
9.tq: Use the event count and exact year to distinguish the second exit from the earlier withdrawal.

9.s: Sarnath was inscribed as India's 45th World Heritage Site at which session and venue?
9.x: Sarnath was inscribed at the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee held in Busan, South Korea, in July 2026. It became India's 45th World Heritage Site and Uttar Pradesh's fourth.
9.tq: Match the site with the correct committee session and venue.

9.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
9.x: The Maratha Military Landscapes of India were inscribed at the 47th session of the World Heritage Committee in Paris in 2025. Sarnath, Hoysala temples and Deepavali are associated with different UNESCO processes and venues.
9.tq: Find the one accurate site–session–venue combination among near-neighbouring UNESCO events.

9.s: The Hoysala temples of Karnataka were inscribed on the World Heritage List in:
9.x: The Hoysala temples of Karnataka were inscribed in September 2023. The year 1983 relates to India's first World Heritage inscription involving Ajanta and Ellora.
9.tq: Distinguish a recent inscription date from the earlier landmark inscription year.

9.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the UNESCO World Heritage List in July 2026:
1. It contained 1,273 properties in 173 countries.
2. The properties included 991 cultural, 240 natural and 42 mixed sites.
3. Italy had the highest number of sites, followed by China.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. Italy had 62 sites and China 61, the two highest national totals in the stated list.
9.tq: Handle a multi-part numerical statement by checking totals, categories and ranking separately.

9.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
9.x: The World Heritage List had 42 mixed properties, not 52. Italy had 62 sites, China 61, and the list included 240 natural properties.
9.tq: Find the altered figure in a numerical table by comparing each category with the stated total.

9.s:
Which of the following statements about UNESCO is correct?
1. Its headquarters is in Paris.
2. India is a founding member.
3. It has 194 members and 12 associate members.
4. Its Executive Board has 58 members.
9.x: UNESCO is headquartered in Paris; India is a founding member; UNESCO has 194 members and 12 associate members; and its Executive Board has 58 members.
9.tq: Use an all-inclusive option only after verifying each institutional fact independently.

9.s: Lucknow was included in UNESCO's Creative Cities Network as a City of:
9.x: Lucknow was named a City of Gastronomy in recognition of Awadhi cuisine at UNESCO's 43rd General Conference in Samarkand in October–November 2025.
9.tq: Match the city with its exact Creative Cities category, not merely its cultural reputation.

9.s:
With reference to Indian entries in UNESCO lists, consider the following statements:
1. Lucknow is India's second City of Gastronomy after Hyderabad.
2. Hyderabad received the designation in 2019.
3. Deepavali was inscribed at the 20th Intangible Cultural Heritage Committee meeting in New Delhi in December 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. Lucknow followed Hyderabad as India's second gastronomy city, while Deepavali was inscribed at the 20th ICH Committee meeting at the Red Fort, New Delhi.
9.tq: Separate World Heritage, Intangible Heritage and Creative Cities categories before selecting the code.

9.s: The first Indian World Heritage site, inscribed along with Ellora, was:
9.x: Ajanta, along with Ellora, was India's first World Heritage site inscription in 1983.
9.tq: Use the historical first rather than the latest inscription in the same subject area.

9.s: Which institution is the nodal agency for World Heritage matters in India and looks after 28 World Heritage properties among 3,688 centrally protected monuments?
9.x: The Archaeological Survey of India is the nodal agency for World Heritage matters and looks after 28 World Heritage properties among 3,688 centrally protected monuments.
9.tq: Identify the responsible authority from its operational role and numerical jurisdiction.

9.s: The Chicago Convention of 1944 is primarily concerned with:
9.x: The Chicago Convention of 1944 governs international civil aviation and led to the creation of the International Civil Aviation Organization.
9.tq: Match each convention with its governing sector rather than its date alone.

9.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Basel Convention — prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals
9.x: The Vienna Convention of 1985 concerns protection of the ozone layer. Rotterdam concerns prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals, Basel concerns transboundary hazardous waste, and the Windsor Framework concerns post-Brexit UK–EU trade rules for Northern Ireland.
9.tq: Discriminate among conventions dealing with closely related environmental and trade subjects.

9.s: The Montreal Protocol of 1987 is associated with:
o: Hazardous chemicals under prior informed consent
9.x: The Montreal Protocol of 1987 regulates ozone-depleting substances and operates in the broader framework of ozone-layer protection.
9.tq: Distinguish the ozone regime from the hazardous-chemical and POPs regimes.

9.s: The Hague Conventions administered through HCCH primarily deal with:
9.x: The Hague Conventions under HCCH concern private international law, including the Apostille Convention of 1961 and the Child Abduction Convention of 1980.
9.tq: Use the subject-area clue to distinguish private international law from public international organisations.

9.s: Which convention governs the transboundary movement of hazardous waste?
9.x: The Basel Convention of 1989 governs transboundary hazardous waste. It also includes a plastic-waste amendment and stronger rules relating to e-waste.
9.tq: Match the convention to its core regulatory object and avoid confusing adjacent environmental treaties.

9.s: The Rotterdam Convention is associated with the principle of:
o: Prior Informed Consent for hazardous chemicals
9.x: The Rotterdam Convention establishes the Prior Informed Consent procedure for certain hazardous chemicals and pesticides in international trade.
9.tq: Recognise the operational principle attached to the convention rather than its general environmental character.

9.s: The Stockholm Convention of 2001 primarily concerns:
9.x: The Stockholm Convention deals with persistent organic pollutants. The listed framework covers 34 chemicals, including recently noted substances such as chlorpyrifos and PFAS.
9.tq: Use the exact environmental category—POPs—to separate Stockholm from Basel and Minamata.

9.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Minamata Convention?
o: Mercury; dental amalgam to be phased out by 2034
9.x: The Minamata Convention of 2013 concerns mercury, and dental amalgam is to be phased out by 2034. POPs belong to the Stockholm Convention and hazardous waste to the Basel Convention.
9.tq: Start from the sure substance–treaty pair and eliminate the swapped environmental categories.

9.s: The Windsor Framework of 2023 governs:
o: UK–EU post-Brexit trade rules for Northern Ireland
The global trade in hazardous chemicals
The admission of new NATO members
9.x: The Windsor Framework establishes UK–EU post-Brexit trade arrangements for Northern Ireland.
9.tq: Identify the geographic and political parties governed by the framework.

9.s:
Arrange the following conventions/frameworks in chronological order of adoption:
A. Minamata Convention
B. Chicago Convention
C. Stockholm Convention
D. Basel Convention
9.x: The correct sequence is Chicago Convention (1944), Basel Convention (1989), Stockholm Convention (2001), and Minamata Convention (2013).
9.tq: Place the earliest and latest dates first, then resolve the middle sequence.

9.s: The WHO Pandemic Agreement was adopted on which date?
9.x: The WHO Pandemic Agreement was adopted on 20 May 2025.
9.tq: Use the exact date to distinguish the treaty from later developments concerning its annex.

9.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the WHO Pandemic Agreement:
1. It was adopted on 20 May 2025.
2. Its PABS annex has already been agreed.
3. Talks on the PABS annex resumed in Geneva in July 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The PABS annex, concerning Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing, was still not agreed.
9.tq: Find the statement that reverses the status of an unfinished international agreement.

9.s: PABS, referred to in connection with the WHO Pandemic Agreement, stands for:
9.x: PABS stands for Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing.
9.tq: Test the exact expansion of a specialised international abbreviation.

9.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Ebola situation in 2026:
1. The outbreak was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in May 2026.
2. The Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda were associated with its spread.
3. By July 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo had 1,561 confirmed cases and 506 deaths.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. Ebola was declared a PHEIC in May 2026, spread from the DRC to Uganda, and the DRC figures by July 2026 were 1,561 confirmed cases and 506 deaths.
9.tq: Use a multi-statement question to combine date, countries and numerical outbreak data.

9.s: The Global Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance for 2026–2036 was adopted at:
9.x: The 79th World Health Assembly, held in May 2026, adopted the Global Action Plan on AMR 2026–2036.
9.tq: Match the initiative with the adopting international forum and year.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Fiji — 26th country to eliminate trachoma, October 2025
9.x: India was certified polio-free in 2014, not malaria-free. Cabo Verde, Fiji and Sri Lanka are correctly matched with the stated certifications.
9.tq: Identify the swapped disease certification in a country–achievement pair.

9.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Country)
 a. Bhutan
 b. Chile
 c. Niger
 d. Timor-Leste

List-II (WHO certification or validation)
 i. Malaria-free
 ii. First in the Americas to eliminate leprosy
 iii. First in the WHO South-East Asia Region to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies
 iv. First in Africa and fifth in the world to end onchocerciasis

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
9.x: Bhutan was the first in the WHO South-East Asia Region to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies; Chile was first in the Americas to eliminate leprosy; Niger ended onchocerciasis; and Timor-Leste became malaria-free.
9.tq: Start from the sure country–certification pair and eliminate the remaining codes.

9.s:
Which of the following country–certification pairs are correctly matched?
1. Fiji — elimination of trachoma in October 2025
2. Timor-Leste — most recent malaria-free certification in July 2025
3. India — polio-free certification in 2014
4. Sri Lanka — malaria-free certification in 2016
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
9.x: All four pairs are correct. Fiji eliminated trachoma in October 2025, Timor-Leste was the most recent malaria-free country in July 2025, India became polio-free in 2014, and Sri Lanka became malaria-free in 2016.
9.tq: Check every row of a certification table before selecting the combined code.

9.s: Wild poliovirus remains endemic only in which of the following countries?
9.x: Wild poliovirus remains endemic only in Pakistan and Afghanistan.
9.tq: Test the exact two-country exception rather than the broader list of previously affected countries.

9.s: Which outbreak-related development was reported in relation to Indonesia?
o: Indonesia became the 26th country to eliminate trachoma
Indonesia was declared free of dog-transmitted rabies
WHO ended Indonesia's type-2 poliovirus outbreak
9.x: WHO ended Indonesia's type-2 poliovirus outbreak. This is distinct from the continuing endemic presence of wild poliovirus in Pakistan and Afghanistan.
9.tq: Distinguish the ended type-2 outbreak from current wild-poliovirus endemicity.

9.s:
Which of the following were elected as non-permanent members of the UN Security Council for 2027–28?

2. Kyrgyzstan
3. Portugal
4. Trinidad and Tobago
5. Zimbabwe

9.tq: Treat a complete membership list as a set and check whether any listed country has been omitted or added.

9.s: The United Nations Security Council consists of:
o: 15 members, comprising 5 permanent and 10 elected members
10 members, comprising 5 permanent and 5 elected members
17 members, comprising 5 permanent and 12 elected members
15 members, comprising 10 permanent and 5 elected members
9.x: The UNSC has 15 members: 5 permanent members and 10 members elected for two-year terms.

9.s: The term of India's elected membership in the UN Human Rights Council is:
9.x: India was elected unopposed to the UN Human Rights Council for 2026–28, for the seventh time.

9.tq: Use the term-length trap by comparing closely related UN memberships.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about India's recent engagement with UN bodies:

2. India was elected unopposed to four ECOSOC subsidiary bodies.
3. India was re-elected to the ICAO Council for 2025–28.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. India chaired the Commission on Narcotic Drugs in March 2025, was elected unopposed to four ECOSOC subsidiary bodies, and was re-elected to the ICAO Council for 2025–28.
9.tq: Combine office held, election status and term information in one coded question.

9.s: Under Article 97 of the UN Charter, the Secretary-General is appointed by:
o: The Economic and Social Council on the recommendation of the Security Council
The UN Security Council on the recommendation of the General Assembly
The International Court of Justice on the recommendation of the General Assembly
The UN General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council
9.x: Article 97 provides for appointment by the UN General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council.
9.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to distinguish recommendation from appointment authority.

9.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 2026 process for appointing the next UN Secretary-General:
1. The appointment is for a term of five years.
2. Straw polls are part of the process.
3. Candidates held UN General Assembly dialogues on 21–22 April 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: The process involves a five-year term, straw polls and UNGA dialogues held on 21–22 April 2026.
9.tq: Check dates and procedural stages separately before choosing the combined option.

The World Summit on the Information Society in Tunis

9.x: The ITU Area Office is located at C-DOT in New Delhi.
9.tq: Use the headquarters and location trap to separate organisations with international offices.

Match List-I with List-II:

 c. UN CERD
 d. WHA79

1. INTERPOL is headquartered at Lyon.
2. The Central Bureau of Investigation is India's National Central Bureau for INTERPOL.
3. The CBI seeks Red Notices.
4. A Blue Notice was issued for the Goa nightclub owners after a fire killed 25 people.

An INTERPOL system for tracing criminal assets
A WEF initiative on global economic restructuring
A UN mechanism for electing non-permanent members

9.x: The Great Reset was a World Economic Forum initiative launched in 2020.

9.s:

2. It entered into force on 17 January 2026.
3. India has ratified the treaty.

9.x: The BBNJ Treaty was adopted in March 2023 and entered into force on 17 January 2026. India has signed but not ratified it.

9.x: India has signed the BBNJ Treaty but has not ratified it.
9.tq: Discriminate between the closely related treaty stages of signature and ratification.

9.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the UN Convention against Cybercrime is correct?
o: India signed it at Hanoi in October 2025.
India did not sign it, citing concerns relating to privacy and data sovereignty.
India ratified it immediately after its adoption in December 2024.
It was negotiated under the International Civil Aviation Organization.
9.x: India did not sign the UN Convention against Cybercrime because of concerns relating to privacy and data sovereignty.
9.tq: Use the country-status and stated-reason trap in an international agreement question.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about the UN Convention against Cybercrime:
1. It is described as the first global cybercrime treaty.
2. It was adopted through UN General Assembly Resolution 79/243 in December 2024.
3. It was opened for signature at Hanoi in October 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. The Convention is the first global cybercrime treaty, was adopted through Resolution 79/243 in December 2024, and opened for signature at Hanoi in October 2025.
9.tq: Check each date, venue and institutional description separately before selecting the coded combination.

9.s: The UN Convention against Cybercrime becomes binding how many days after the deposit of the 40th ratification?
9.x: The Convention becomes binding 90 days after 40 ratifications have been deposited.

9.x: The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) serves as the secretariat of the Convention against Cybercrime.
9.tq: Apply the ‘which international body performs this function?’ method.

9.x: The First Additional Protocol concerns electronic certificates of origin.

9.x: The PABS annex, concerning pathogen access and benefit-sharing, is associated with the WHO Pandemic Agreement. The Windsor Framework concerns Northern Ireland trade, while the Washington Accords concern DRC-Rwanda peace.
9.tq: Use the subject-based matching method and eliminate swapped agreements.

9.s: The WHO Pandemic Agreement was adopted by the World Health Assembly on
9.x: The WHO Pandemic Agreement was adopted by the World Health Assembly on 20 May 2025.

9.x: PABS means pathogen access and benefit-sharing. Its annex was still under negotiation during the Geneva talks in July 2026.

9.x: India backs the developing-country Group for Equity in the negotiations on the WHO Pandemic Agreement.
9.tq: Identify the correct negotiating group rather than a similarly named international grouping.

9.x: The Chicago Convention of 1944 created the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).
9.tq: Match a founding convention with the organisation it created.

9.x: India was re-elected to the ICAO Council for the 2025-2028 period.
9.tq: Distinguish the exact institutional term from nearby three-year periods.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about the Water Convention:
1. It was adopted at Helsinki in 1992.
2. It entered into force in 1996.
3. It concerns transboundary rivers and lakes.
4. Bangladesh became the first South Asian party.

9.x: All four statements are correct. The Helsinki Water Convention was adopted in 1992, entered into force in 1996, concerns transboundary waters, and Bangladesh was the first South Asian party.

9.s: The Washington Accords, signed on 4 December 2025, concern
o: the regulation of high seas biodiversity
trade between the United Kingdom and the European Union
peace between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda
9.x: The Washington Accords are a United States-brokered peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda.

o: UK-EU arrangements on Northern Ireland trade
the conservation of high seas biodiversity
9.x: The Windsor Framework, concluded in 2023, is a UK-EU arrangement concerning trade in Northern Ireland.

9.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Convention on Nuclear Safety — India became a party in 2016
Convention on Supplementary Compensation — India became a party in 2016
Convention on Supplementary Compensation — adopted in 1997; entered into force in 2015
Convention on Nuclear Safety — adopted in 1994; entered into force in 1996

9.tq: Find the swapped date or status in a set of closely related nuclear conventions.

9.s: With reference to the five United Nations outer-space treaties, which one of the following is correct regarding India?
o: India has ratified all five but signed only four.
India has signed and ratified all five.
India has signed all five and ratified four, but not the Moon Agreement of 1979.
India has neither signed nor ratified the Moon Agreement but has ratified only three others.
9.x: India has signed all five UN outer-space treaties and ratified four. The exception is the 1979 Moon Agreement, which India has not ratified.

9.s: Which one of the following statements about the Montreal Protocol is correct?
o: It was replaced by the Chicago Convention in 2026.
It has been ratified by 90 parties and is not universally ratified.
It has been ratified by 197 parties and is universally ratified.
India will stop all HFC production immediately under the original protocol.

9.s: Under the Kigali Amendment, India will stop clearances for new HFC production beyond
9.x: India will stop clearances for new hydrofluorocarbon production beyond 31 December 2027 under the Kigali Amendment.

9.s: In January 2026, the United States announced its exit from how many organisations and treaties in total?
9.x: The United States announced its exit from 66 organisations and treaties: 35 non-UN and 31 UN entities or instruments.

the first country to ratify it
the first country to attempt formal withdrawal from it

o: appoint the secretariat of every UN convention
ratify every treaty without executive action
withdraw India from any treaty without consultation
legislate for implementing treaties and international agreements
9.x: Article 253 empowers Parliament to make laws for implementing treaties, agreements and conventions with foreign countries or decisions made at international conferences.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

9.x: The India-UK CETA was signed in July 2025 and entered into force on 15 July 2026.

The India-EU FTA was signed with EFTA as its partner.
