It has prohibited customs duties on electronic transmissions since 1998 and lapsed on 31 March 2026.
9.x: The moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions had existed since 1998 and lapsed for the first time on 31 March 2026.
9.tq: Separate the exact subject, duration and outcome instead of relying on a familiar WTO term.

9.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Investment Facilitation for Development (IFD) proposal at WTO MC14?
o: It was rejected by the WTO Secretariat before the conference.
It was backed by 129 of 166 members but was not added to Annex 4 after India blocked it.
It was added to Annex 4 unanimously.
It was backed by 66 members and adopted as a plurilateral agreement.
9.x: Although 129 of the 166 members supported it, India blocked adding the IFD agreement to Annex 4.
9.tq: Check the difference between broad support and actual adoption.

9.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. MC9 — Bali — Peace Clause for food-security stockholding
2. MC12 — Geneva — Fisheries Subsidies Agreement, Phase 1
3. MC13 — Abu Dhabi — 26 February to 2 March 2024
4. MC14 — Yaoundé — 26 to 29 March 2026
9.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. MC9 was held in 2013, MC12 in 2022, MC13 in 2024 and MC14 in 2026.
9.tq: Start from the sure venue-year pair and verify each conference outcome.

9.s:
Arrange the following WTO events in chronological order:
A. MC12 adopted Phase 1 of the Fisheries Subsidies Agreement.
B. MC9 adopted the Peace Clause for food-security stockholding.
C. MC14 was held at Yaoundé.
D. MC13 was held at Abu Dhabi.
9.x: The correct order is MC9 in 2013, MC12 in 2022, MC13 in 2024 and MC14 in 2026.
9.tq: Fix the earliest and latest conferences first, then place the middle events by year.

9.s: Which of the following statements about WTO Ministerial Conferences is correct?
o: It was created after the Doha Round was concluded.
It functions under the IMF and deals exclusively with exchange rates.
It is the WTO's highest body and meets at least once every two years under the Marrakesh Agreement.
It is an advisory body that meets once every five years.
9.x: The WTO Ministerial Conference is the organisation's highest decision-making body and meets at least every two years.
9.tq: Identify the authority and function of the institution rather than its latest event.

9.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Doha Round — concluded successfully before MC14
MC12 — Geneva — Fisheries Subsidies Agreement, Phase 1
9.x: The Doha Round has never concluded. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
9.tq: Find the reversed or overstated conclusion in a list of familiar WTO facts.

9.s: The BRICS New Delhi Declaration of September 2026 called for which of the following reforms?
o: A permanent ban on all WTO dispute settlement proceedings
Abolition of the IMF and World Bank
IMF and World Bank quota and voting reform and restoration of the WTO Appellate Body
Replacement of the WTO by a BRICS-only trade organisation
9.x: The declaration sought reform of IMF and World Bank quotas and voting, along with restoration of the two-tier WTO dispute-settlement system.
9.tq: Link a declaration with its specific institutional demands.

9.s: The headquarters of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is located at:
9.x: UNEP is headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya.
9.tq: Use the headquarters-location association for international organisations.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
9.x: UNESCO is headquartered in Paris. WHO is in Geneva, FAO in Rome and ILO in Geneva.
9.tq: Start from a certain headquarters pair and eliminate swapped locations.

9.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. UNESCO was established in 1945.
2. UNESCO has 194 members and 12 associate members.
3. Its Executive Board consists of 58 members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct: UNESCO dates from 1945, has 194 members and 12 associate members, and has a 58-member Executive Board.
9.tq: Test date, membership and composition together, with the complete combination as an option.

9.s: Who among the following is the Director-General of the World Health Organization?
9.x: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus is the Director-General of WHO, whose headquarters is in Geneva.
9.tq: Discriminate between heads of closely related international organisations.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
9.x: IAEA is headed by Rafael Grossi. Arsenio Dominguez is the Secretary-General of the IMO, headquartered in London.
9.tq: Find the wrong head attached to an otherwise plausible headquarters pair.

9.s: Qu Dongyu, the Director-General of the FAO, belongs to which country?
9.x: Qu Dongyu is from China. India is also a founding member of FAO.
9.tq: Use nationality as the decisive discriminator among organisation heads.

9.s: Which of the following statements regarding the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) is correct?
o: It is headquartered in London and deals with maritime affairs.
It was established in 1865, is the oldest UN agency, has 194 members, and India joined in 1869.
It was established in 1944 and India joined it in 1945.
It is headquartered in Montreal and has a 36-member Council.
9.x: ITU was established in 1865, is the oldest UN agency, has 194 members and India joined in 1869.
9.tq: Combine establishment year, membership and India-specific chronology to identify the precise option.

9.s: The 36-member Council is associated with which organisation?
9.x: ICAO, established in 1944 under the Chicago Convention, has a 36-member Council and is headquartered in Montreal.
9.tq: Match the distinctive numerical composition with the correct organisation.

9.s: Which one of the following statements about the International Monetary Fund is correct?
o: It is headquartered in Shanghai and has no country veto.
It is headquartered in Washington, D.C., and formally came into existence on 27 December 1945.
It was established by the Fortaleza Declaration of 2014.
It was established under the Chicago Convention in 1944.
9.x: The IMF is headquartered in Washington, D.C.; it originated at Bretton Woods in 1944 and formally came into existence on 27 December 1945.
9.tq: Distinguish the IMF from other institutions by headquarters and founding chronology.

9.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. New Development Bank — Shanghai — no country holds a veto
2. UNFCCC Secretariat — Bonn — 198 Parties
3. UN Alliance of Civilizations — New York — established in 2005 by Türkiye and Spain
9.x: All three pairs are correct. The New Development Bank dates from 2014, while the UN Alliance of Civilizations was launched in 2005 by Türkiye and Spain.
9.tq: Verify the repeated headquarters pattern before checking the institutional details.

9.s:
Which of the following organisations are headquartered in Geneva?
1. WHO
2. ITU
3. WMO
4. WTO
5. ILO
9.x: WHO, ITU, WMO, WTO and ILO are all headquartered in Geneva.
9.tq: Group organisations by a common headquarters and test the complete set.

9.s: The Secretary-General of the International Maritime Organization is:
9.x: Arsenio Dominguez of Panama is the Secretary-General of IMO, headquartered in London.
9.tq: Apply the head-to-organisation matching method using nearby international-office holders as distractors.

9.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the proposed transition of the United Nations Secretary-General's office?
o: The successor takes office only after approval by the IMF.
Guterres demits office at the end of 2026, and the successor's five-year term begins on 1 January 2027.
Guterres demits office in 2025, and the successor's term begins in August 2026.
The successor is elected directly by the Security Council for a four-year term.
9.x: António Guterres is scheduled to demit office at the end of 2026; the successor's five-year term is to begin on 1 January 2027.
9.tq: Separate office-holder, transition date and term length from the appointment procedure.

9.s: The election of Khalilur Rahman as the 81st UN General Assembly President represented the turn of which regional group?
9.x: The 2026–27 presidency was the turn of the Asia-Pacific Group. Khalilur Rahman defeated Cyprus.
9.tq: Link a regional rotation with the office-holder rather than confusing it with nationality alone.

9.s: Which one of the following nationality pairs is correctly matched?
o: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus — Ethiopia; Qu Dongyu — China
Celeste Saulo — Panama; Arsenio Dominguez — Argentina
Qu Dongyu — Argentina; Celeste Saulo — China
9.x: Tedros is Ethiopian and Qu Dongyu is Chinese. Celeste Saulo and Rafael Grossi are Argentine, while Arsenio Dominguez is Panamanian.
9.tq: Use paired nationalities to eliminate deliberate cross-swaps among organisation heads.

9.s: The International Solar Alliance was launched by which countries at COP21 in 2015?
9.x: The International Solar Alliance was sponsored by India and France at COP21 in 2015; its secretariat is at Gurugram.
9.tq: Match an initiative with its founding sponsors and launch occasion.

9.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the International Solar Alliance is correct?
1. It is open to all UN members.
2. Its secretariat is located at Gurugram.
3. Romania ratified its Framework Agreement in 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. The Alliance is open to all UN members, has its secretariat at Gurugram and received Romania's ratification in 2026.
9.tq: Combine objective, location and recent membership-related development in one coded question.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kimberley Process — conflict-diamond certification — no headquarters
Global Biofuels Alliance — India's G20 — biofuels
9.x: CDRI was sponsored by India in 2019 and is headquartered in New Delhi. Japan and Tokyo are not its sponsor and secretariat combination.
9.tq: Detect the swapped sponsor and location in an initiative-based pairing.

9.s: The Kimberley Process is primarily associated with:
9.x: The Kimberley Process, established in 2003 by governments, industry and civil society, operates the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme for conflict diamonds and has no headquarters.
9.tq: Infer the initiative from its stated objective rather than from its institutional participants.

9.s: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) is jointly sponsored by:
9.x: The IPCC is sponsored by UNEP and WMO. Its AR6 synthesis report was released on 20 March 2023, and its AR7 cycle began in July 2023.
9.tq: Match the scientific body with its sponsoring organisations.

9.s: Which one of the following correctly describes POWERR Asia?
o: A Japan-sponsored initiative under AZEC Plus, launched in April 2026 for energy resilience, with India as a participant
A UNEP climate assessment cycle beginning in July 2023
An India-sponsored food-security programme launched at WTO MC14
An FAO treaty on plant genetic resources
9.x: POWERR Asia was sponsored by Japan under AZEC Plus in April 2026, focuses on energy resilience and includes India as a participant.
9.tq: Combine sponsor, framework, date, objective and participation in a single identification question.

9.s: The International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture, also known as the “Seed Treaty”, is sponsored by:
9.x: The ITPGRFA is sponsored by FAO and concerns plant genetic resources in harmony with the Convention on Biological Diversity.
9.tq: Use the common name and objective to identify the sponsoring organisation.

9.s: Which United Nations peacekeeping mission is located in South Sudan, with its headquarters at Juba?
9.x: UNMISS is the United Nations Mission in South Sudan and is based at Juba.
9.tq: Expand the acronym and match it with the host country.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about UNMISS:
1. It operates in South Sudan.
2. India is its largest troop contributor, with 1,775 troops.
3. Two hundred and ten Indian peacekeepers received the UN Medal in August 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. UNMISS is in South Sudan, India is its largest troop contributor with 1,775 troops, and 210 Indian peacekeepers received the UN Medal in August 2026.
9.tq: Test mission location, troop contribution and a numerical recent-development detail together.

9.s: UNIFIL is associated with which of the following locations?
o: The Golan Heights, where it began in 1974
South Sudan, where it began in 2011
The Democratic Republic of the Congo, where it began in 1999
Lebanon, where it has operated since 1978
9.x: UNIFIL is the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon and has operated there since 1978. An end to the force has been forecast.
9.tq: Distinguish peacekeeping acronyms by host country and start date.

9.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: MONUSCO — Democratic Republic of the Congo
9.x: MONUSCO operates in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. UNDOF is associated with the Golan Heights in Syria, UNIFIL with Lebanon and UNMISS with South Sudan.
9.tq: Use the sure acronym-country pair and eliminate host-country swaps.

9.s: The United Nations Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) is deployed in:
o: The Democratic Republic of the Congo
9.x: UNDOF is deployed in the Golan Heights, Syria.
9.tq: Test the expansion of the acronym against the distinctive geographic location.

9.s: Which WTO subsidy box covers trade-distorting domestic support that is subject to a cap based on de minimis limits?
9.x: Amber Box subsidies are trade-distorting domestic support measures and are subject to prescribed limits, including de minimis ceilings.
9.tq: Use the exact subject-function association to distinguish the subsidy boxes.

9.s: Support tied to production-limiting programmes is classified under which WTO subsidy box?
9.x: Blue Box support is linked to programmes that limit production.
9.tq: Discriminate between the closely related Amber, Blue and Green subsidy categories.

9.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Green Box measures are regarded as having minimal or no trade distortion.
2. Green Box support is not subject to a cap.
3. Green Box measures are exclusively related to intellectual property rights.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: Green Box measures have minimal or no trade-distorting effects and are not capped. Intellectual property rights are covered by TRIPS, not the Green Box.
9.tq: Find the statement that swaps a subsidy category with a neighbouring WTO agreement.

9.s: TRIPS, an agreement administered within the WTO framework, primarily deals with:
9.x: TRIPS stands for Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights.
9.tq: Test the expansion and precise subject of a commonly confused acronym.

9.s: TRIMs is concerned with:
9.x: TRIMs refers to Trade-Related Investment Measures.
9.tq: Separate look-alike WTO acronyms by their exact subject.

9.s: Which one of the following statements regarding GATT is correct?
o: It was signed in 1994 and came into force in 1995.
It was signed in 1947 and came into force in 1948.
It was signed in 1986 and came into force in 1991.
It was signed in 1948 and came into force in 1947.
9.x: The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade was signed in 1947 and entered into force in 1948.
9.tq: Use the chronological pair to catch a reversal of the signing and enforcement years.

9.s: GATT originally had how many parties when it was established?
9.x: GATT had 23 original parties.
9.tq: Recall the specific founding number rather than confusing it with institutional membership figures.

9.s: The Most-Favoured-Nation clause is associated with which of the following?
9.x: The Most-Favoured-Nation clause is a fundamental principle associated with GATT.
9.tq: Match a distinctive principle with the correct international agreement.

9.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Uruguay Round was the eighth round of multilateral trade negotiations under GATT.
2. It commenced in 1986.
3. It resulted in the creation of the WTO on 1 January 1995.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: The Uruguay Round was the eighth GATT round, began in 1986 and led to the WTO, which came into existence on 1 January 1995.
9.tq: Combine the round number, starting year and institutional outcome in one statement set.

9.s: Which of the following subjects was included among the major outcomes of the Uruguay Round?
o: Farm subsidies, services and intellectual property
9.x: The Uruguay Round addressed agriculture and farm subsidies, trade in services and intellectual property rights, among other matters.
9.tq: Identify the option containing the complete cluster of related subjects.

9.s: The Dunkel Draft of 1991 was associated with proposals made by:
9.x: The Dunkel Draft contained proposals made by Arthur Dunkel, the Director-General of GATT, during the Uruguay Round.
9.tq: Use the person–institution–document association rather than a general economic personality link.

9.s: The Peace Clause agreed at Bali in 2013 primarily protects developing countries from WTO disputes concerning:
9.x: The Bali Peace Clause shields developing countries' public food-stockholding programmes from disputes over Amber Box limits until a permanent solution is found.
9.tq: Apply the agreement to the specific policy situation it was designed to protect.

9.s: The Bretton Woods Conference was held in:
9.x: The Bretton Woods Conference took place in 1944. Its ideas were associated with Harry Dexter White and John Maynard Keynes.
9.tq: Distinguish the conference year from the later establishment and operational years of the institutions.

9.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
9.x: The IMF formally came into existence on 27 December 1945, while its operations began on 1 March 1947.
9.tq: Separate closely spaced institutional dates by matching each date with the correct event.

9.s: The first borrower from the International Monetary Fund was:
9.x: France was the first country to borrow from the IMF.
9.tq: Test the specific first-institutional-event fact against nearby country names.

9.s: The headquarters of the International Monetary Fund is located in:
9.x: The IMF headquarters is in Washington, D.C.
9.tq: Use the headquarters-location association and avoid swapping it with other international organisations.

9.s: Which institution generally provides loans for middle-income countries' public infrastructure?
9.x: The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development provides loans mainly for public infrastructure in middle-income countries.
9.tq: Distinguish the mandates of the World Bank Group institutions and the IMF.

9.s: Long-term interest-free credits and grants for health and primary education are characteristic of:
9.x: The International Development Association provides long-term interest-free credits and grants, including for health and primary education.
9.tq: Match the concessional financing instrument with the correct World Bank institution.

9.s: Which of the following is the private-sector arm of the World Bank Group?
9.x: The International Finance Corporation is the private-sector arm of the World Bank Group and has 184 members.
9.tq: Identify the institutional mandate hidden among similar abbreviations.

9.s:
Consider the following statements about IMF lending:
1. The IMF lends only to its member countries.
2. Its lending is intended to address balance-of-payments problems.
3. The Rapid Financing Instrument requires a full economic programme in every case.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: The IMF lends only to members and primarily addresses balance-of-payments problems. The Rapid Financing Instrument provides quick liquidity without requiring a full programme.
9.tq: Locate the reversed condition in a statement about an institutional lending instrument.

9.s: The IMF loan facility described as providing quick liquidity without a full programme, including during disasters, pandemics and post-conflict situations, is:
9.x: The Rapid Financing Instrument provides rapid liquidity without a full programme in emergencies such as disasters, pandemics and post-conflict situations.
9.tq: Match the emergency scenario with the facility designed for rapid access to funds.

9.s: Which IMF facility was associated with the softest terms?
9.x: The Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility, or ESAF, had the softest terms among the facilities mentioned.
9.tq: Distinguish concessionality from speed and from the mandates of other institutions.

9.s: During the 1991 crisis, India received approximately what amount from the IBRD and IMF combined?
9.x: India received approximately $7 billion from the IBRD and IMF during the 1991 crisis, followed by the New Economic Policy.
9.tq: Select the specific historical financial figure rather than a later programme amount.

9.s: Which combination best describes the structural adjustment programmes of the 1980s and 1990s?
o: Debt cancellation, disarmament and refugee resettlement
Public food stocking, tariff abolition and gold accumulation
Universal subsidies, nationalisation and currency appreciation
9.x: Structural adjustment programmes commonly involved austerity, privatisation and devaluation; studies linked them to rising poverty and inequality in the Global South.
9.tq: Identify the complete policy cluster associated with structural adjustment programmes.

9.s: The Amaravati Capital City Development Programme, including flood works such as the Undavalli pumping station, is associated with:
9.x: The programme is in Andhra Pradesh and includes flood works with an 8,400-cusecs Undavalli pumping station.
9.tq: Start from the sure project–state pair and reject similar state-level projects.

9.s: The World Bank-supported AP Road Sector Project covers approximately:
o: 850 km of major district roads and State highways
9.x: The AP Road Sector Project covers about 850 km of major district roads and State highways in Andhra Pradesh.
9.tq: Use the project’s distinctive length and road classification to eliminate altered figures.

9.s: SALT, or Supporting Andhra's Learning Transformation, is a project financed by the:
9.x: SALT is a World Bank-supported education project in Andhra Pradesh.
9.tq: Match the programme acronym with its lender and sector.

9.s: Mission Schools of Excellence, involving AIIB and World Bank financing of ₹7,500 crore, is associated with:
9.x: Mission Schools of Excellence is associated with Gujarat and involves AIIB and World Bank financing of ₹7,500 crore.
9.tq: Combine the project, lender pair and State instead of relying on the project name alone.

9.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: NDB — SALT programme in Andhra Pradesh
IBRD — Mission Schools of Excellence in Gujarat
9.x: AIIB is associated with Mumbai Urban Transport Project-III. NDB is associated with the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS, while SALT is a World Bank project in Andhra Pradesh.
9.tq: Catch the lender–project swap by comparing neighbouring multilateral-bank projects.

9.s: The Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut Regional Rapid Transit System is financed by:
9.x: The Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS is associated with NDB financing in collaboration with ADB and serves the National Capital Region.
9.tq: Identify the correct lender partnership rather than a single-bank association.

9.s: The NDB-supported Major District Roads project is associated with which State?
9.x: The Major District Roads project supported by NDB is in Madhya Pradesh.
9.tq: Match the road project with the correct State from the project table.

9.s: The IBRD programme for the Green Hydrogen Mission amounts to approximately:
9.x: IBRD is associated with a $1.5 billion national programme for the Green Hydrogen Mission.
9.tq: Distinguish a programme-specific amount from unrelated trade and crisis figures.

9.s: Approximately how much was facilitated by the Centre for Amaravati through the World Bank, ADB and HUDCO?
9.x: The Centre facilitated approximately ₹26,000 crore for Amaravati through the World Bank, ADB and HUDCO; ₹15,000 crore was separately fast-tracked as special assistance.
9.tq: Separate the total facilitated amount from the distinct special-assistance component.

9.s: Under the voting arrangement of the New Development Bank, the founders' collective vote cannot fall below:
9.x: The founders' vote in the New Development Bank cannot fall below 55%.
9.tq: Recall the institutional safeguard percentage rather than selecting a round distractor.

9.s: Which one of the following statements about the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank is correct?
o: It was established in 2014 and has 55 approved members.
It was established in 2016 and has 111 approved members.
It was established in 2023 and has 184 approved members.
It was established in 1995 and has 29 approved members.
9.x: AIIB was established in 2016 and has 111 approved members.
9.tq: Match the institution’s founding year with its membership figure.

9.s: The BRICS Contingency Reserve Arrangement is intended to serve as:
o: A mechanism for intellectual property registration
A common agricultural subsidy fund of the WTO
An alternative source of IMF-type liquidity support for BRICS members
9.x: The BRICS Contingency Reserve Arrangement provides a BRICS alternative to IMF liquidity support.
9.tq: Infer the institutional purpose from the type of financial problem addressed.

9.s: Which of the following is a Maastricht criterion for entry into the Eurozone?
o: Public debt below 20% of GDP only
9.x: Eurozone entry criteria include a deficit below 3% of GDP, debt below 60% of GDP and participation in ERM II.
9.tq: Recognise the precise numerical threshold among reversed or incomplete criteria.

9.s: According to the stated development, which country became the 21st member of the Eurozone in 2026?
9.x: Bulgaria became the 21st member of the Eurozone in 2026 after meeting the Maastricht criteria.
9.tq: Test the newest-member fact against nearby European countries.

9.s: India became the world's fourth-largest economy in 2025 in terms of nominal GDP, with a size of approximately:
9.x: India was reported as the fourth-largest economy in 2025 with a nominal GDP of approximately $4.18 trillion, overtaking Japan.
9.tq: Link the ranking with the specific nominal GDP figure rather than a trade value.

9.s: India was ranked third globally when GDP was measured on the basis of:
o: Purchasing power parity, based on ICP 2021
9.x: India was the third-largest economy by purchasing power parity according to the ICP 2021 measure.
9.tq: Separate nominal GDP ranking from PPP ranking.

9.s: India's reported position in the IMF ranking after the fall in the rupee was:
9.x: India was reported to have slipped to sixth place in the IMF ranking after the rupee's fall.
9.tq: Distinguish a later ranking change from the earlier fourth-place nominal GDP report.

9.s: India overtook Russia to become the fourth-largest holder of foreign exchange reserves, with reserves of approximately:
9.x: India's foreign exchange reserves were reported at approximately $785.71 billion, placing it fourth after China, Japan and Switzerland.
9.tq: Combine the rank, amount and comparison countries to identify the correct reserve figure.

9.s: In July 2026, Russia accounted for more than what share of India's oil imports?
9.x: Russia supplied more than 51% of India's oil imports in July 2026, an all-time high in the stated period.
9.tq: Distinguish the July peak from the earlier sub-20% share in January.

9.s: Which statement correctly describes India's commercial-services trade in 2024?
o: India was the fourth-largest exporter with a 15.73% share and the sixth-largest importer with an 8.85% share.
India was the ninth-largest exporter with a 3.4% share and the eighth-largest importer with a 4.3% share.
India was the eighth-largest exporter with an 8.85% share and the ninth-largest importer with a 15.73% share.
India was the eighth-largest exporter with a 4.3% share and the ninth-largest importer with a 3.4% share.
9.x: In 2024, India was the eighth-largest exporter of commercial services with a 4.3% share and the ninth-largest importer with a 3.4% share.
9.tq: Check both rank–share pairs and avoid reversing exporter and importer positions.

9.s: Which country was India's largest import source in 2024–25 among the following?
9.x: China was India's largest listed import source in 2024–25, accounting for 15.73%, followed by Russia, the UAE and the United States.
9.tq: Compare the percentages rather than relying on the geopolitical prominence of a country.

9.s: India's record remittances in FY 2024–25 were reported at approximately:
9.x: India received record remittances of approximately $135 billion in FY 2024–25.
9.tq: Distinguish the annual remittance total from the separate workers' remittance measure for FY26.

9.s: Foreign direct investment inflows in 2025 increased by 73% to approximately:
9.x: FDI inflows increased by 73% in 2025 to approximately $47 billion.
9.tq: Match the percentage increase with the correct resulting inflow amount.

9.s: India's current account deficit was reported at approximately what amount in the first quarter of FY 2027?
9.x: India's current account deficit was reported at approximately $4.2 billion in Q1 of FY 2027.
9.tq: Distinguish the current account figure from FDI, IMF assistance and infrastructure programme amounts.

9.s:
With reference to the World Economic Outlook, consider the following statements:
1. The January 2026 update raised India's FY26 growth projection to 7.3% from 6.6%.
2. The April 2026 reference scenario projected global growth at 3.1%.
3. The April 2026 projection for India in FY27 was about 6.2%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All three statements are correct. The IMF's January 2026 update raised India's FY26 projection to 7.3%, while its April 2026 reference scenario projected global growth at 3.1% and India's FY27 growth at about 6.2%.
9.tq: Use the numerical comparison of successive projections and check all statements against the same report series.

9.s: The World Economic Outlook is published by which of the following organisations?
9.x: The World Economic Outlook is an IMF publication. The World Bank publishes the Global Economic Prospects, UN DESA publishes the World Economic Situation and Prospects, and the ILO publishes Employment and Social Trends.
9.tq: Match the report with its publishing institution rather than with a related economic body.

9.s: The April 2026 World Economic Outlook projected global growth at what rate if the West Asia war deepened?
9.x: The April 2026 WEO projected global growth at 2.0% in the event of a deepening war, compared with 3.1% in its reference scenario.
9.tq: Separate the reference scenario from the adverse scenario before selecting the figure.

9.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Global Economic Prospects, June 2026:
1. It is published by the World Bank.
2. It is issued twice a year.
3. It projected India's FY27 growth at 6.6%, up from 6.5%.
4. It projected world growth at 2.5%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
9.x: All four statements are correct. The June 2026 Global Economic Prospects is a twice-yearly World Bank publication and gave the stated India and world growth projections.

The transfer of Chabahar to the United States

Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Conflict or dispute — Parties or location

India deployed Navy escort missions named Sankalp and Urja Suraksha.
India joined the US–Israel attacks on Iran.

Makes all Indian systems exclusively French

Visakhapatnam under the Eastern Naval Command
Port Blair under the Andaman and Nicobar Command

A burrowing frog from the urban landscape of Karnataka
A freshwater flowering plant from Telangana

Match List-I with List-II:

12.s: Rakthamichthys anchi, reported in August 2026, is a:

Blind, blood-red swamp eel found in dug-out wells of Goalpara, Assam
Deep-sea skate from the Arabian Sea

12.s: Simonia lawbah is significant because it represents:
o: The first deep-sea skate discovered under the Deep Ocean Mission
India's first species of the Mesalina genus
The first wolf snake from Great Nicobar Island
India's first species of the Simonia genus

12.s: Mesalina bishnoi, reported in June 2026, is associated with which of the following?
o: A swamp eel from Assam associated with dug-out wells
A lizard from Rajasthan, representing the first Mesalina genus record in India and honouring the Bishnoi community
A wolf snake from Great Nicobar Island named after Irwin
A lichen-forming fungus from the Western Ghats named after a botanical institution

12.s: Ammannia telanganensis is a freshwater flowering plant reported from:
o: Alpine meadows of Jammu and Kashmir
Ranga Reddy wetlands and Amrabad Tiger Reserve in Telangana
12.x: Ammannia telanganensis was reported from the Ranga Reddy wetlands and Amrabad Tiger Reserve in Telangana in August 2026.
12.tq: Use the habitat and State together to distinguish a plant discovery from aquatic and cave species.

12.s: Dipturus dhritiae, reported in September 2026, is associated with which one of the following?
o: A ray spider from a cave in Meghalaya named after a local community
A lizard from Rajasthan named after the Bishnoi community
A deep-sea skate from the Arabian Sea named after Dhriti Banerjee
A wolf snake from Great Nicobar Island named after Irwin

12.s: Lycodon irwini, reported in 2025, was discovered in:

12.tq: Use the common name and island location as the decisive clues.

12.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Five Allographa species — Lichen-forming fungi of the Western Ghats

12.s: The International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) is correctly described as:

An India-led, treaty-based alliance headquartered in New Delhi
A Brazil-led forest fund headquartered in Brasília
A UAE–Indonesia initiative headquartered in Jakarta

The Deep Ocean Mission and the Zoological Survey of India
The National Mission for Clean Ganga and the Ministry of Jal Shakti
Germany's International Climate Initiative and COP28
